articles.title: Salario mínimo en Colombia: Consejo de Estado alista fallo clave que puede cambiarlo todo sobre el incremento
articles.standfirst: Tensión por el salario mínimo: Petro convoca a huelga general ante inminente fallo del Consejo de Estado
articles.summary: Tensión por el salario mínimo: Petro convoca a huelga general ante inminente fallo del Consejo de Estado
articles.body: La puja por el incremento del salario mínimo en Colombia entra en su fase más crítica. La Sección Segunda del Consejo de Estado cerró formalmente la etapa de pruebas y unificó en un solo expediente las múltiples demandas presentadas por gremios económicos y ciudadanos contra la norma que fijó el ajuste salarial para el año 2026. Con esta decisión, el alto tribunal dejó listo el borrador que determinará la legalidad del decreto emitido por el Ejecutivo. El centro del litigio jurídico se enfoca en las demandas acumuladas contra el Decreto 0159 de 2026, el cual fijó el salario mínimo mensual en $1.750.905. Los demandantes argumentan que el ajuste decretado contravino los parámetros legales de la negociación tripartita y superó los límites de inflación y productividad, comprometiendo la sostenibilidad de las pequeñas y medianas empresas. La revisión judicial gira en torno al marco normativo que estableció el salario mínimo mensual en $1.750.905 (tras haberse decretado un incremento inicial del 23 %). El avance del proceso en los estrados judiciales provocó una fuerte reacción política por parte del expresidente Gustavo Petro. A través de su cuenta en la red social X, el exmandatario cuestionó severamente la independencia del Consejo de Estado y advirtió que revocar la cifra fijada impactará directamente el poder adquisitivo de las familias trabajadoras. "Trabajadores de Colombia, el Consejo de Estado hoy es una oficina de la Casa de Nariño, lástima, pero aquí revocaron el salario mínimo vital que es el mínimo ingreso que garantiza la vida de cualquier familia trabajadora y de todas con una sola firma de un burócrata adinerado...", manifestó Petro en su mensaje. El expresidente sostuvo que tumbar el denominado "salario vital" destruirá el consumo interno, llevando al empresariado a la quiebra y arriesgando a la clase media a caer nuevamente en la pobreza. Asimismo, equiparó las eventuales repercusiones de la decisión judicial con un escenario de "bancarrota" e inestabilidad social. Ante el inminente pronunciamiento de la magistratura, Petro elevó la tensión institucional haciendo un llamado directo a la movilización masiva y a la huelga general. La convocatoria no estuvo dirigida exclusivamente a las centrales obreras tradicionales, sino que buscó involucrar a trabajadores informales, del campo y del sector servicios. "No llamo solo a las centrales obreras, llamo al trabajador y trabajadora de la calle y del campo y del taller y la oficina a moverse, a mover el esqueleto por el derecho al salario vital. Le declaran la guerra al pueblo trabajador y el pueblo trabajador debe responder con millones de personas en las calles hacia la huelga general...", concluyó. El Consejo de Estado no ha anunciado una fecha exacta para la notificación oficial de la sentencia. No obstante, tras la unificación del expediente, la decisión definitiva podría conocerse en cuestión de días, en medio de una fuerte expectativa económica y una creciente polarización en el debate público nacional. Con la etapa probatoria formalmente cerrada, la Sección Segunda del Consejo de Estado se alista para expedir la sentencia definitiva. El fallo definirá si el decreto guarda plena conformidad con los principios constitucionales o si, por el contrario, requiere ajustes o anulaciones, en un ambiente de marcada polarización política y amenaza de paros nacionales.

articles.title: Where did Williams’ $1M worth F1 car go? Team sues garage owner for $1M+ after Ralf Schumacher historic car’s mystery disappearance
articles.summary: Williams is taking legal action against former garage owner Peter Thorpe after a historic Formula 1 car allegedly disappeared.
articles.body: Williams is taking legal action against former garage owner Peter Thorpe after a historic Formula 1 car allegedly disappeared. The British team is seeking £1 million ($1.34 million) from Thorpe for the return of its rare FW23, valued at £750,000 ($1.01 million). The car was driven by Ralf Schumacher and Juan Pablo Montoya during the 2001 F1 season.The FW23 was loaned to Autotech Performance Ltd in 2015. It was supposed to be displayed at the company’s garage in Telford. Williams later asked for the car to be returned, but the team says it received no response. Autotech has since been liquidated and dissolved.Williams seeks return of its missing FW23 car or $1.3 millionWilliams says the FW23 is part of its unique collection of heritage Formula 1 cars. Only nine examples of the car were manufactured. The team claims it strictly controls the use and sale of its historic cars to help preserve them.According to Williams’ court case, the team loaned the car to Autotech in 2015 under a “Historic Car Loan Agreement.” The agreement allowed the company to keep the car until October 2021.Williams then contacted Autotech that year and asked to inspect the car. The team also terminated the loan. However, it says there was no response.Williams’ lawyers claim the car was later removed from the garage. They allege Thorpe wrongly told a valuer working on Autotech’s liquidation that he personally owned the vehicle.“The car is part of the claimant’s unique collection of its own heritage cars, the use or sale of which it strictly controls inter alia [among other things] to ensure so far as possible that they are preserved”, Williams’ barrister Richard Clegg said while setting out the claim in the case papers.He added, “In 2015, the claimant agreed to loan the car to Autotech on the terms of a document entitled “Historic Car Loan Agreement” which terms were known and agreed to by Autotech.”Williams also claims the car remained at the company’s premises until its voluntary liquidation. The team says the vehicle was removed sometime after the liquidation process began.Thorpe, however, strongly disputes the allegations. He says he does not know where the car is and denies telling anyone that he owned it.His lawyer Duncan MacPherson said, “He does not know who in fact owned the car then or now. The defendant closed the business of Autotech on 30 June 2021. The defendant suffered a stroke on 7 October 2018 that caused him cognitive impairment,”Thorpe says he last saw the FW23 at the premises on August 8, 2021, when Autotech’s assets were being valued.His defence states, “The defendant admits that the car was at the premises on 8 August 2021, but does not admit whether it remained there until December 2021, because this lies outside his knowledge.”He also said he “believes that he has not told anyone that he owned the car, because he knew this to be untrue”.The case was filed at the High Court in London. It has not yet reached a full trial. articles.title: “We’re committed to helping find a cure”: Triple H and wife Stephanie McMahon’s Pittsburgh fund Connor’s Cure raises $4.6M for 500 families
articles.summary: Triple H and his wife Stephanie McMahon founded Connor’s Cure in 2014 to honor late WWE fan, Connor Michalek.
articles.body: Triple H and his wife Stephanie McMahon founded Connor’s Cure in 2014 to honor late WWE fan, Connor Michalek. The Pittsburgh-based fund supports pediatric cancer research and families worldwide.Connor was diagnosed with medulloblastoma at age 3. He inspired the WWE fraternity through his unbreakable courage and unforgettable connection to his hero and retired professional wrestler, Daniel Bryan.The Connor’s Cure initiative partnered with UPMC Children’s Hospital of Pittsburgh, and later with The V Foundation. Together, they could fund groundbreaking pediatric cancer research, including studies on DIPG [childhood diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma] and solid tumors.Through these futuristic efforts, Connor’s Cure has raised more than $4.6 million and helped over 500 families worldwide since its launch in April 2014. Stephanie McMahon and husband Triple H founded Connor’s Cure to honor Connor MichalekConnor’s Cure was inspired by Pittsburgh native Connor Michalek. When he was 3 years old, he was diagnosed with medulloblastoma, a tumor of the brain and spinal cord. He received a lifetime amount of radiation and underwent several surgeries. Doctors gave him a 0% chance of survival. He began clinical trials.In October 2012, a YouTube video of Michalek went viral in which he requested to meet his hero, then-WWE professional wrestler Daniel Bryan.Hundreds of people joined a Facebook group called “Help Connor meet Daniel Bryan.” Within 2 days, then-WWE chairman and CEO Vince McMahon responded that Bryan would meet Michalek.Twice, they met - once in December 2012 and a second time in October 2013. Michalek became a regular fixture at subsequent WWE events. WWE invited him to WrestleMania XXX. He scored a pinfall victory over Triple H and saw Bryan win the WWE World Heavyweight Championship in early April 2014.In late April 2014, Michalek passed away at the age of 8. He left a lasting impression on everyone he met in the WWE sphere. He was known for a quick wit and infectious grin. He melted even the toughest hearts of the WWE superstars and divas.Stephanie McMahon and her husband Paul Levesque became passionate about pediatric cancer research after meeting WWE superfan Connor “The Crusher” Michalek.A month after Connor passed away, Paul “Triple H” Levesque and Stephanie McMahon founded Connor’s Cure fund at Children’s Hospital of Pittsburgh to honor his irreplaceable spirit.The WWE and Connor’s Cure raise funds to support pediatric cancer research. Donations to Connor’s Cure fund pediatric brain and spinal cancer research and medical care for children and their families.In 2016, Connor’s Cure raised almost $1 million. That same year, Connor’s Cure and UPMC Children’s Hospital of Pittsburgh grew their partnership by joining forces with The V Foundation for Cancer Research. This partnership continued to drive research breakthroughs so no child would suffer as much as Connor Michalek did.Following The V Foundation’s partnership, support from the Connor’s Cure fund expanded nationwide to additional prominent researchers and cancer centers desperately seeking a cure for pediatric cancer.The UPMC Children’s Hospital of Pittsburgh was named to the prestigious U.S. News & World Report Best Children’s Hospitals Honor Roll for 2026-2027.The hospital earned a place in the nation’s top 10 pediatric hospitals.The hospital also ranked in all 11 pediatric specialties surveyed. The hospital leads the nation in pediatric care, research, innovation, and education.WWE and The V Foundation advance the fight against childhood cancerThe V Foundation for Cancer Research, a top-rated cancer research charity, announced $16.2 million in funding awarded to 18 exceptional scientists through its Dick Vitale Pediatric Cancer Research Fund.Vitale and WWE have combined their efforts to fund three pediatric V Foundation Translational Grants totaling $1.8 million. Of that amount, Vitale and WWE contributed $900,000.Translational Grants are three-year awards totaling $600,000. They support bench-to-bedside research. Two of the grants will fund studies related to DIPG [childhood diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma], a universally fatal brain cancer. The third grant will fund research for solid tumors in children.“We’re thrilled to team with Dick Vitale to help further critical research and studies that are necessary in the fight against pediatric cancer,” Stephanie McMahon said via The V Foundation website.“Through WWE’s partnership with The V Foundation and in honor of Connor Michalek, we are committed to continue helping find a cure and will not stop until we do.”“Words cannot describe the excitement and joy I am feeling learning that Stephanie McMahon and her WWE team have united with us in providing funding that will play a vital role in battling pediatric cancer,” Dick Vitale said.“It is simply amazing what they are doing to attack the cancers that have caused nightmares for many youngsters and their families. These grants are made possible by the generosity of WWE and the kindness and generosity of those who have donated to our gala.We feel confident that these research grants will make a difference in the outcome for children with cancer.”The V Foundation has awarded more than $250 million for cutting-edge cancer research, holds a four-star rating from Charity Navigator, and is among the top 3% of all charities evaluated.WWE has also produced the “Support Tomorrow’s Superstars” campaign for pediatric patients undergoing treatment, supporting children fighting cancer.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: “You Gotta Be More Disciplined”: Rob Gronkowski Criticizes Mike Vrabel After Patriots HC’s Unsportsmanlike Conduct in Week 4
articles.summary: Mike Vrabel has witnessed several referees make many bad calls. And the Week 4 game between the New England Patriots and the Buffalo Bills was one such game.
articles.body:
Mike Vrabel has witnessed several referees make many bad calls. And the Week 4 game between the New England Patriots and the Buffalo Bills was one such game. However, when the head coach confronted the referee for the bad call, the league turned against him with some disciplinary actions.

Days later, former Patriots star Rob Gronkowski weighed in on the scenario. He acknowledged that the penalty's fairness depended on exactly what Vrabel said to the referee. Gronkowski wondered what would happen if Vrabel had confronted the referee in the XFL, where coaches and referees can exchange words without penalty. He believed that it'd be quite appealing. But reality was different.

"What if Vrabel and this referee just started going at it and there was no consequences for Vrabel? That would be fun to watch," Gronkowski said on The Gronk & Jules Show . "But you can't. You gotta be disciplined. That doesn't set a good example. I don't care if this referee deserved it or not. You got to be more disciplined, and then it sets an example for your players, like, 'Oh, our coach got a personal conduct penalty. Why can't we?'

"In this case, it must have gotten them fired up because they won this game… In this case, it was good. That's good coaching right there."

This incident happened when the referee called a defensive holding on cornerback Marcus Jones against wide receiver D.J. Moore in the second quarter of the game. Even though the pass was incomplete, the penalty gave the Bills a fresh set of downs. Ultimately, it ended with a touchdown for Buffalo.

Vrabel was pretty upset with the call. And cameras caught him shouting that it was a "terrible call" with some expletive words. As a result, Vrabel received an unsportsmanlike conduct penalty for shouting expletives at the referee on the sideline.

Vrabel, however, later addressed the incident in his postgame press conference . He clarified that as a head coach, he had told referees about their bad calls 87 times. The head coach even claimed that there was "nothing derogatory" about his comments. And that prompted him to believe that the referee was a bit too "sensitive." Nevertheless, he knew that he shouldn't have used expletive words.

"I probably shouldn't have swore, but I could tell you that in my history of being on the sidelines as a head coach, I've said that and I apologize to him," Vrabel said. "And again, the players responded. It was unfortunate. And I have to be better in those moments."

Meanwhile, PFWA pool reporter and ESPN's Mike Reiss interviewed the referee, Vill Vinovich, following the game. After explaining what happened, Vinovich weighed in on whether the league could have given Vrabel a warning instead of a penalty.

"I don't know how you're going to give a warning," the referee told Reiss. "It's not something that is going to happen twice. When you use language like that, it's pretty much a given."

Well, getting slapped with an unsportsmanlike conduct penalty contradicts the elite discipline that the Patriots need to maintain their winning culture. Even though the Patriots secured a 29-26 win, Vrabel's conduct will remain a lesson for the team to stay calm under pressure.

articles.title: Padres Going With Seasoned Veteran As Game 4 Starting Pitcher vs. Brewers
articles.summary: The San Diego Padres are sending Walker Buehler to the mound for Game 4 of the NLDS against the Milwaukee Brewers.
articles.body: It's Walker Buehler's turn to keep the San Diego Padres' season alive. Following its Game 3 win over the Milwaukee Brewers in the National League Division Series on Tuesday night, San Diego announced that Buehler will start Game 4 on Wednesday night (10 p.m. ET on FS1). Buehler missed Games 1 and 2 of the series, as he was placed on the paternity list. He was activated Monday, taking the place of fellow right-hander Randy Vásquez on San Diego's roster. Buehler made 32 starts for the Padres in the regular season, his most in a single season since 2021 — a year that saw the right-hander earn his second All-Star nod with the Los Angeles Dodgers (2019 was his other All-Star campaign). Over said outings, Buehler recorded a 4.63 ERA, a 1.35 WHIP and an 88 ERA+, while totaling 131 strikeouts and 0.9 strikeouts over 153 ⅔ innings pitched. The 32-year-old Buehler has made 18 starts and 19 appearances altogether in the postseason, all of them coming with the Dodgers, with whom he spent the first seven seasons of his big-league career (2017-22 and 2024). Buehler boasts a career 3.04 ERA and 1.15 WHIP in the playoffs, while totaling 114 strikeouts over 94 ⅔ innings pitched. The Padres went 4-2 against the Brewers in the 2026 regular season and are now a combined 4-0 at home against Milwaukee, which hasn't yet named a starter for Game 4. Prior to the divisional round, San Diego swept the Chicago Cubs in the Wild Card Series, out-scoring Chicago 12-1. Regarding Game 3, Padres ace Michael King pitched the final two innings, getting a game-ending double play after putting two runners on the basepath in the top of the ninth. King pitching the ninth inning was partially a result of superstar closer Mason Miller, ironically, being placed on the paternity list before Game 3 and, therefore, unable to pitch. The Padres, who trail the Brewers in the series 2-1, are seeking their first trip to the NL Championship Series since 2022. Should San Diego pull off the series comeback, it would face the winner of the NLDS matchup between the Dodgers and Atlanta Braves in the NLCS.

articles.title: Justin Verlander Reflects On 21-Year MLB Career And Emotional Decision To Retire
articles.summary: Justin Verlander officially retired from the MLB after spending 21 seasons in the league. Now that his Hall of Fame playing career is behind him, it didn’t take long before he made his return to the sport.
articles.body: Justin Verlander officially retired from MLB after spending 21 seasons in the league. Now that his Hall of Fame playing career is behind him, it didn’t take long before he made his return to the sport. Verlander joined the "MLB on FOX Pregame" crew on Tuesday night alongside Kevin Burkhardt, Derek Jeter, Alex Rodriguez and David Ortiz. Making his TV studio debut, he opened up about his decision to retire and reflected on what went into finally calling it a career. "It was pretty easy," Verlander said. "I made my first start of the season and my leg started hurting. I’ve said my entire career, man, I love this game. I love giving it everything I got. I’m going to play until the wheels fall off. The arm held out great, but the leg gave out on me." It’s hard to imagine a more fitting farewell to Verlander’s legendary career. As he prepared to walk off the mound for the last time after allowing two runs over 5 ⅓ innings with six strikeouts, the 43-year-old was greeted by his daughter on the field. The two hugged, causing Verlander to start visibly crying with his teammates surrounding him on the mound – making for an unforgettable, emotional moment between father and daughter. If Verlander was going to say goodbye to the game for good, it’s the kind of fairytale ending almost every pitcher dreams of. "It still hits me," Verlander said. "There’s so many thoughts going through your head, obviously just leading up to such an emotional weekend. Then to just be completely blindsided and look over and see my daughter running at me. It obviously hit me and it was pretty special." Verlander leaves behind an exceptional legacy. Over his 21 seasons in the league, he built a Hall of Fame résumé highlighted by two World Series titles, three Cy Young Awards and an American League MVP. However, what Verlander reflected on most was his durability and ability to maintain an elite workload year after year. "I'm most proud of the volume," explained Verlander, who threw 3,802 ⅔ innings between the regular season and postseason in his career. "I really pride myself on taking the ball and just being out there for as many pitches as the game would allow. When I look back, I always said that if I’m out there for every start the numbers fall where they may, but [at least] I’m doing my job." Verlander has given more to the game than most, becoming one of just 19 pitchers in MLB history to play 21 seasons or more. As he steps off the mound for good, fans can look forward to seeing him share his insights from behind the analyst desk.

articles.title: El emotivo llanto de Juan Manuel Rengifo tras debutar con la Selección Colombia
articles.standfirst: El jugador de Atlético Nacional rompió en lágrimas al finalizar el encuentro contra Perú
articles.summary: El jugador de Atlético Nacional rompió en lágrimas al finalizar el encuentro contra Perú
articles.body: La victoria 2-0 de la Selección Colombia frente a Perú en el Nu Stadium de Miami dejó sensaciones muy positivas en el terreno de juego y una imagen cargada de emotividad para la historia del fútbol nacional: el atacante Juan Manuel Rengifo, una de las grandes promesas del recambio generacional, rompió en llanto al finalizar el encuentro, superado por la emoción de haber sumado sus primeros minutos con la camiseta tricolor de la absoluta. Rengifo, quien ingresó desde el banco al inicio del segundo tiempo en reemplazo de Yáser Asprilla, fue determinante en la dinámica ofensiva del equipo dirigido por Néstor Lorenzo. Su presencia le dio dinamismo al ataque cafetero y aportó la asistencia para el primer gol de la noche, obra del lateral Samuel Velásquez al minuto 57. Posteriormente, Daniel Arcila selló el triunfo definitivo en el tiempo de adición (90+2') tras una brillante maniobra individual. Al término del pitazo final, la tensión contenida y la magnitud del logro afloraron. Rengifo cayó de rodillas al césped estadounidense y no pudo contener las lágrimas mientras festejaba con sus compañeros, en un gesto espontáneo que rápidamente se volvió viral en las redes sociales. Al término del partido, el centrocampista compartió sus sensaciones sobre lo que significó estrenarse a nivel internacional con el equipo mayor, destacando el trasfondo emocional que acompaña este logro en su carrera. “Soy un poco llorón, yo vivo mucho esto. El fútbol es mi vida y poder seguir cumpliendo sueños desde mi debut en Atlético Nacional, mi primer gol y todo lo que he vivido allá, y ahora el sueño de poder vestir la Tricolor, de poder representar a este país que tanto uno ama.” Este encuentro amistoso le sirvió al cuerpo técnico nacional para dar rodaje a nuevas alternativas en el frente de ataque y consolidar variantes de cara a los próximos retos oficiales. El llanto de Rengifo refleja el sentimiento de una nueva generación de futbolistas que sueñan con consolidarse en el combinado patrio y ganarse un lugar definitivo en el proceso camino a las próximas competencias internacionales.

articles.title: Who is DonnaJean Wilde? Meet the 61-year-old grandmother who broke the women’s plank world record with a 5-hour hold
articles.summary: DonnaJean Wilde apparently decided four and a half hours in a plank was not enough.
articles.body: DonnaJean Wilde apparently decided four and a half hours in a plank was not enough.The 61-year-old Canadian grandmother has reportedly raised her own mark to five hours, according to the World Senior Games. Wilde previously earned Guinness World Records recognition after holding an abdominal plank for four hours, 30 minutes and 11 seconds in March 2024.Who is DonnaJean Wilde, the 61-year-old grandmother behind the 5-hour plank world record?Wilde is a former high school vice principal and teacher from Alberta, Canada. She is also a mother of five and grandmother of 12.Her connection with planking started long before world records entered the picture.According to Guinness World Records, Wilde began planking after suffering a wrist injury that prevented her from running or lifting weights. She found that the static exercise was something she could still perform.Wilde later told Impact Magazine that the injury changed the direction of her training."I couldn't run. I could hardly walk down the road with a sling, but I could plank. It was such a pivotal moment for me that day. It just changed my life," she said.Her family eventually began testing how long she could stay in the position. During the COVID-19 pandemic, Wilde reached two hours.That result pushed the challenge into much more serious territory.She began structured preparation for the record in 2023. Her training included planks, running, weight lifting and push-ups, according to Impact Magazine.On March 21, 2024, Wilde held a plank for four hours, 30 minutes and 11 seconds at Magrath High School, her former workplace.Guinness World Records recognized the performance as the longest time in an abdominal plank position by a woman. She beat the previous record, held by fellow Canadian Dana Glowacka, by more than 10 minutes.Wilde told Guinness that even after completing the attempt, the result was difficult to process."I actually still can't believe it," she said. "It feels like a dream."Two years later, the World Senior Games reported that Wilde had pushed the mark even further with a five-hour plank.How did DonnaJean Wilde train her body to hold a plank for five hours?Five hours did not come from doing planks alone.Wilde has said she uses several forms of strength training, including push-ups, weight lifting and running. She has also added dead hangs to her routine.In an Instagram post about upper-body strength, Wilde said she performs hundreds of push-ups and credited dead hangs with improving her grip.That matters because Wilde has dealt with chronic pain and numbness in her hands. Guinness previously reported that she lives with discomfort in her hands and arms.Her training volume before the 2024 record was far beyond a normal fitness routine. Guinness reported that Wilde sometimes practiced planking for as long as six hours per day while preparing for the attempt.And the plank is not her only record-setting exercise.In 2024, Wilde completed 1,575 push-ups in 60 minutes, breaking the existing record of 1,207 at the time. That mark has since been surpassed, according to Women’s Health.Her approach also comes with an important distinction. Wilde has trained for extreme endurance over several years. Her routine is not a starting point for an average person trying to improve core strength.Wilde’s own advice is much simpler."Keep trying and keep practicing," she told Guinness after her 2024 plank record.At 61, she is apparently still following it herself.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Roll The Tape: Will Mike Macdonald Again Get The Best Of Kyle Shanahan?
articles.summary: After diving into the All-22 coaches' film from Week 4, Bucky Brooks examines four new developments to watch.
articles.body: The Dallas Cowboys just saved their season. The Chicago Bears are surviving without Caleb Williams. The Jacksonville Jaguars are the biggest surprise in the AFC. And the San Francisco 49ers and the Seattle Seahawks have picked up right they left off last year. Each week, I dive into the All-22 coaches' film before offering a few insights to watch. Here are four developments that could be long-term storylines involving some of the best teams and players in the NFL. 1.How The Seahawks Have Consistently Shut Down The 49ers If you enjoy watching a chess match on artificial turf, you might want to tune in when the San Francisco 49ers take on the Seattle Seahawks on Sunday (4:25 p.m. ET on FOX) for the battle of wits between Kyle Shanahan and Mike Macdonald. As brilliant schemers with voluminous playbooks loaded with creative play designs from various personnel groupings, the whiteboard matchup will showcase the imagination and innovative tactics of two of the league’s best coaches. The 46-year-old Shanahan has revolutionized football with variations of a zone-based scheme popularized by his legendary (and Super Bowl-winning) father, Mike. The 49ers' run-heavy formations are built on off-tackle plays perfectly complemented by exotic pre-snap shifts, motions and condensed alignments. With the constant movement and misdirection leaving defenders dazed and confused, San Francisco routinely generates explosive plays on blown assignments and misalignments. The 39-year-old Macdonald, though, has often neutralized the Niners by featuring two-high safeties, light boxes and various sub-package personnel with five or six defensive backs on the field. Additionally, Seattle varies its adjustments to motions to give the quarterbacks false keys on whether the coverage is man or zone based on defensive backs running across the formation. The Seahawks will occasionally run their defenders across the field, shadowing the motion man before dropping into zone coverage. They will also "rock-and-roll" defenders and meet the motion man on the other side in man coverage. The ever-changing tactics and intricate pre-snap disguises prevent the 49ers from exploiting the "tells" opponents give away with their alignments. With the Seahawks stockpiling interchangeable, versatile defensive backs, light boxes let the "Dark Side" use the speed and quickness of their hybrid defenders to contain the run while staying over the top of play-action passes. To accomplish this, the Seahawks rely heavily on their imposing defensive line to control the point of attack, with Leonard Williams, Byron Murphy II and Jarran Reed whipping blockers with their individual and collective athleticism and physicality. The trio's explosiveness clogs interior gaps and forces the 49ers to the edges against a group of fast defensive backs who excel at one-on-one tackles in space. As Macdonald preaches a "12 as one" mentality throughout his team, the Seahawks’ defense takes the mantra a step further by playing like an extra defender is on the field through their effort and physicality between the lines. Against the 49ers, the Seahawks rely on that energy and flawless execution to match up with an offensive juggernaut that features blue-chip players at every marquee position, including quarterback (Brock Purdy), running back (Christian McCaffrey), wide receiver (Mike Evans), tight end (George Kittle) and left tackle (Trent Williams). The 49ers’ offense has been rolling with its stars and veteran role players (see: Deebo Samuel and Kyle Juszczyk), making key plays in pivotal moments in a scheme that puts defenders in a mental and physical grinder. The complex shifts, motions, and condensed alignments force quick adjustments, while the downhill running game and "catch-and-run" aerial attack test every defender's open-field tackling skills and overall physicality. While Macdonald has typically gotten the upper hand against Shanahan — his defenses have held the Niners to less than 20 points in five of six meetings, including without a touchdown in their past two encounters — the first edition of their 2026 heavyweight battle will feature a few new tricks and tactics that keep the defensive guru running to the tablet to see how the offensive wizard is creating extra gaps in the running game and free access for his playmakers on passing plays. Given Shanahan’s attention to detail in crafting a game plan that meshes an ultra-physical rushing attack with a razzle-dazzle passing game, Macdonald will need to come up with another masterpiece to cool off the league’s hottest team. 2.Why CeeDee Lamb Might Be The Best Receiver In Football While there is no disputing George Pickens and CeeDee Lamb as the most dynamic pass-catching duo in football, No. 88 is making a run at the NFL’s top spot overall. He's strung together three 100-yard games, putting him atop the league's leaderboard in receptions (37) and receiving yards (498) through four games. He is also tied for second in big plays (receptions of 20-plus yards) with seven. Such numbers are even more impressive when considering Lamb is in a playmaker-by-committee situation with Pickens roaming the opposite side of the field. Lamb is coming off his best game yet, collecting 17 catches for 189 yards and a jaw-dropping go-ahead touchdown against the Texans that showcased his spectacular route-running skills. Although the three-time All-Pro is an unstoppable force on the perimeter, the Cowboys’ coaching staff has set him up for success by putting him in motion to give him free access to his routes. Per Next Gen Stats, Lamb has been targeted on 46.2% of his routes this season when put in motion, the fourth-highest rate among wide receivers with at least 10 such routes. Additionally, Lamb has generated the third-most yards after the catch (164), while tying for the fourth-most missed tackles among wide receivers. As a former punt returner with exceptional balance and body control, Lamb can elude and evade defenders in space, making him nearly impossible to contain in a scheme that keeps him moving from various alignments. With an emerging superstar on the opposite side commanding double coverage, the Cowboys have found creative ways to get Lamb his touches without disrupting the offensive flow. Moreover, they've put one of the league’s premier playmakers in a prime position to dominate the game and re-emerge as WR1 in a league loaded with blue-chip pass catchers. With Lamb on pace to notch his sixth straight 1,000-yard season and remaining a model of consistency on the perimeter, he might be primed to claim the crown as the league’s top playmaker. 3.How Ben Johnson Has Turned The Bears Into A Ground-And-Pound Machine Bears head coach Ben Johnson has been celebrated as an offensive wizard since building Jared Goff and the Detroit Lions into a juggernaut during his tenure as OC, but the innovative playcaller deserves Bill Walsh-like treatment for transforming the Bears into a ground-and-pound machine that can light up scoreboards with or without Caleb Williams on the field. While Johnson is properly recognized for his work as a quarterback-friendly schemer who can help former No. 1 overall picks maximize their talent and potential, he has quietly crafted some of the league’s most explosive rushing attacks with creative playcalls and exotic formations. After terrorizing opponents with an uptempo, three-receiver offensive package in Detroit that featured multiple running backs and wide receivers shuttling in and out of the game, he has crafted an electric offense in the Windy City that use deception, misdirection and creative personnel deployment to befuddle defensive coordinators around the league. The Bears are among the league leaders in "12" (one running back, two tight ends and two wide receivers) and "13" (one running back, three tight ends and one wide receiver) usage, with tight ends Cole Kmet, Colston Loveland, and Sam Roush taking turns threatening the defense with their dual-threat capabilities as dynamic pass catchers and rugged in-line blockers. Although the Bears like to use the illusion of run-heavy formations to create explosive opportunities in the passing game, their heavy use of multi-tight end sets is part of a shell game that keeps defensive coordinators guessing when running backs D’Andre Swift and Kyle Monangai are on the field. The duo has helped the Bears lead the NFL in rushing (196.3 rush yards per game), while doing most of their damage from spread formations against light boxes. Despite featuring run-heavy formations prominently in their game plans, the explosive plays and spectacular runs are coming on wide-zone plays with one tight end or fewer on the field. Additionally, the Bears have used more under-center formations, particularly with Williams on the sidelines, to enhance their potent running game with a complementary bootleg and play-action package. With backside defenders unable to aggressively chase off-tackle runs to the opposite side of the field, Swift and Monangai have found plenty of creases and seams on impromptu cutback runs. As carefully scripted game plans mix under-center formations, multiple tight-end groupings and perimeter runs, the Bears’ superior talent and tactics are producing explosive runs and time-consuming drives. For a team that loves to dominate opponents with physicality and pizzazz, the Bears’ high-powered offense has old-school football fans singing Johnson’s praises as an offensive guru with a throwback call sheet. 4.The Secret To The Jaguars' Defensive Success If you are scratching your head and wondering how the Jaguars have quickly emerged as title contenders under Liam Coen, you should take a long, hard look at a turnover-obsessed defense that specializes in stopping the run and taking the ball away. Since the start of the 2025 season, Jacksonville has forced 39 turnovers (tied with the Bears for the most during that time) while registering 13 multiple-takeaway games. Given the impact of turnovers on game outcomes, the Jags’ success in knocking the ball loose or picking off passes is directly tied to their ability to win. They led the league in points off takeaways in 2025 — 110 points off 31 turnovers — and they have continued to take advantage of the extra possessions and prime field position this season. Part of the Jaguars' success comes from their ability to stop the run and force opponents into long-yardage situations. Defensive linemen DaVon Hamilton, Josh Hines-Allen and Travon Walker, along with linebackers Foye Oluokun and Ventrell Miller, clog the holes at the point of attack, creating more opportunities to attack the quarterback in obvious passing situations. Jacksonville is stout against the run because of its discipline and physicality in the trenches. The front line avoids "hero" plays that leave open gaps when defenders chase the ball instead of squatting in the hole and waiting for the runner to come back to them. As a result of its disciplined approach, Jacksonville has not allowed even a 75-yard rusher in 21 straight games — the fourth-longest streak in the Super Bowl era. Studying the All-22 coaches’ footage, the Jaguars’ eye discipline and violent hands show up in every clip, with 11 defenders attacking blockers on the way to the ball. The organized approach and "hustle-hard" mentality that demands defenders finish at the ball carrier create a swarming unit that rarely concedes big plays on the ground. In pass coverage, Jacksonville's reliance on zone-based concepts lets second- and third-level defenders keep their eyes on the quarterback, leading to more aggressive breaks on the ball. Additionally, the "vision-and-break" philosophy provides defenders with more chances to snag interceptions off tipped passes or overthrown balls in their areas. With ball-hawking defenders such as Travis Hunter, Jourdan Lewis, Antonio Johnson and Jarrian Jones able to convert errant passes into turnovers, the Jaguars have snagged six interceptions, including three in the red zone. Although the Jaguars’ vision-and-break tactics and "bend but don’t break" philosophy have frustrated some fans who prefer man coverage and a more aggressive approach, their disciplined defenders continue to come up with timely takeaways when the field shrinks and pressure from a persistent pass rush ramps up in pivotal moments. With the umbrella coverage also limiting the "explosives" (passes over 20 yards) that directly lead to points or scoring chances, the Jaguars have kept points off the board — they rank second in scoring defense (13.25 points per game) — and produced the turnovers needed to beat title contenders. As the defense continues to follow second-year defensive coordinator Anthony Campanile’s teachings, the Jaguars are quietly becoming a championship-caliber unit that can spark a title run.

articles.title: Cody Rhodes Reveals New WWE Contract in Surprising Way and Opens Up About Retirement Timeline
articles.summary: Cody Rhodes announced a new contract with WWE, while also discussing his future plans for retirement during an interview this week.
articles.body:
Cody Rhodes announced a new contract with WWE, while also discussing his future plans for retirement during an interview this week.

Appearing Wednesday on Flagrant (h/t Steve Carrier of Ringside News), Rhodes divulged that he "just re-signed" with WWE and will "end [his] wrestling career" with the company:

Rhodes noted that although he "used to have a number in mind" for retirement, his outlook has changed to some degree because watching former wrestlers such as Bobby Roode and Michael Hayes thrive as producers has made him realize he can still be part of WWE and the wrestling business even in retirement.

The American Nightmare went on to tell Flagrant (h/t H Jenkins of Ringside News) that his in-ring retirement "probably will happen sooner than later."

Rhodes added, "When my daughter is 11 years old, I'm not going to be falling down for a living anymore."

The 41-year-old Rhodes has been back with WWE since 2022 after playing a pivotal role in the creation of AEW.

Since returning to WWE, Rhodes has consistently been in or around the world title scene, headlining WrestleMania on multiple occasions, and holding the WWE Championship three times.

It is fair to say Rhodes is still at the top of his game, and the fact that he re-signed with WWE suggests that there are still several big matches and moments in his future.

Multiple big names in WWE have announced their retirement over the past year, including John Cena, AJ Styles and Brock Lesnar.

They were able to step away because the company has been left in good hands with Rhodes, Roman Reigns and so many up-and-coming stars.

While Rhodes is needed as one of the faces of WWE right now, by the time he is ready to retire, there is a good chance the likes of Oba Femi, Bron Breakker, Trick Williams and others will be prepared to take the proverbial torch.

articles.title: Two star pitchers are facing the choice between being on the mound or in the delivery room. It’s not an easy decision
articles.summary: In October, baseball players facing the bright lights of the playoffs must make difficult decisions constantly – on the field and off.
articles.body: With less than an hour to go before a playoff game with their season on the line, the San Diego Padres announced star closer Mason Miller wouldn’t be available. It was shocking, a move that could have potentially derailed the Padres’ attempt to stave off elimination as they faced a 2-0 deficit in their best-of-five National League Divisional Series against the Milwaukee Brewers. Miller and his wife, Jordan, are expecting their first child and Jordan went into labor on Tuesday just hours before Game 3 of the series. Faced with choosing between being available for his team and being present with his wife as their family grew, Miller chose to stay with Jordan and skip the game. On the other side of the country, as his team got ready to play in a similar elimination game, New York Yankees starter Max Fried found himself facing a similar dilemma. Fried and his partner are expecting their first child this week, coinciding with Fried starting a Game 3 elimination contest in which the Tampa Bay Rays could knock the Yankees out of the playoffs and end their season. The Yankees’ hurler was just as sure as Miller what he would do – he was going to be on the mound. Such is life in October for baseball players facing the bright lights of the playoffs, when difficult decisions must be made constantly on and off the field as the long baseball season comes to an end. For the Padres’ closer, the choice was clear – he’d be with his wife over the team. The Millers announced in April that Jordan was pregnant with their first child. According to the San Diego Tribune, Miller told reporters over the weekend that the baby wasn’t expected for a couple more weeks and he hoped the team would be in San Diego when the time came so he didn’t have to make a last-second flight back home. Miller was adamant then that he’d pick being with his wife over the Padres, if it came down to that. He really hoped it wouldn’t. And yet, it did. “Mason got a hold of us early afternoon, right when he would probably come to the ballpark. He was kind of monitoring the situation and just deciding if he’s going to come today or things were going to happen. He decided that he needed to stay with his wife,” Padres manager Craig Stammen told reporters after the game. “We knew sometime in the afternoon, but we wanted to give him enough time in case the baby comes really quick, or it goes the other way, and he could come to the game. We gave him the opportunity. We waited until an hour a half, an hour before the game time to make the final call.” Professional athletes have to make “family or team” decisions all the time, choosing between being there for family or for the team. And in so many cases, the pressure from fans, media, teammates, coaches and front offices, lead to athletes choosing the game over their families. For so many average dads, it might seem like an open-and-shut decision to choose family at a time as monumental as childbirth. But when your job means you have the hopes and dreams of millions of fans riding on your shoulders – well, there’s a bit more gray area in that black-and-white choice. Just ask Fried. Fried and his long-term girlfriend, Reni Meyer-Whalley, are expecting their first child any day, the Yankees pitcher confirmed on Tuesday. When asked whether the uncertainty complicates his thought process around whether to start Game 3 of the Yankees’ ALDS series against the Tampa Bay Rays, Fried was unequivocal. “No. I’ve got a really supportive family that understands that this is my job, and it’s not going to affect what happens tomorrow,” he told reporters, adding later that he planned to start on Wednesday regardless of what’s happening away from the park. Fried is surely hoping for a best-case scenario – pitching on Wednesday night and having his child arrive afterward, making the decision much easier about whether to be in the delivery room or on the mound. As of Wednesday afternoon, there was no word that anything had changed Fried’s mind ahead of the 8 p.m. ET start to Game 3. For Miller, much is still unknown. After Michael King, the starter in Game 2, pitched in Miller’s spot late in Game 3 and helped the Padres to a 4-3 win that extended their season to another night, Stammen said he didn’t know if the fire-throwing closer would return for Wednesday night’s contest. “I think Mason will make that public whenever they have a baby and everything’s good to go,” Stammen said.

articles.title: Yankee Stadium Quietly Suffered a Summer Peanut Shortage
articles.summary: The Yankees mysteriously ran out of peanuts this summer.
articles.body:
Just in time for Game 3 of the American League Divisional Series on Wednesday night in the Bronx, the Yankees say they've solved their summer peanut shortage.

Fans who attended a game at Yankee Stadium in August or September may have noticed peanuts were difficult to find. For weeks at the end of the summer, the classic ballpark snack was unavailable at most locations throughout the stadium.

"We had delays in receiving product toward the end of the summer," a Yankees spokesperson told Front Office Sports.

Legends Global—the food and hospitality company that services Yankee Stadium and is jointly owned by the Yankees, Jerry Jones, and private equity firm Sixth Street—called it a "temporary disruption" from Bazzini, the nut conglomerate, and told FOS it "supplemented with other brands of peanuts starting in late August" to make up for the shortage.

All 30 MLB ballparks sell peanuts. Bazzini declined to comment for this story.

Jeff Sunday, a pseudonymous sports betting influencer, noticed the peanut shortage on Sept. 22 when he attended a Yankees game. He says multiple concession workers told him they had not had any peanuts in stock for about a month. A video he recorded at the game includes a vendor saying, "We haven't had any for the last few home stands."

When FOS attended the Red Sox–Yankees wild-card game Sept. 30, no peanuts could be found anywhere on the 300 seating level, and two food workers said the ballpark was still all out.

"I went to like four different locations looking for peanuts, and everyone I asked was confused," Sunday told FOS. "Clearly there wasn't some memo sent around explaining it to all the ballpark workers."

Legends Global says Yankee Stadium will be fully stocked with Bazzini peanuts for the rest of the playoffs—which may be only one more game.

articles.title: New WWE Rumors on Potential WrestleMania 45 Location for 2029 Event
articles.summary: WWE's WrestleMania may be coming back to New Orleans in the not-too-distant future.
articles.body:
WWE's WrestleMania may be coming back to New Orleans in the not-too-distant future.

Fightful's Sean Ross Sapp reported Wednesday that WWE and the city of New Orleans currently have a hold on the Caesars Superdome for the spring of 2029, which is when WrestleMania 45 would be scheduled to take place.

That news comes just days before WWE is set to stage one of its other biggest premium live events, Money in the Bank, at New Orleans' Smoothie King Center on Saturday.

WrestleMania 42, which was held earlier this year at Allegiant Stadium in Las Vegas, was originally announced for New Orleans back in February 2025.

However, WWE announced a few months later that New Orleans would no longer be the host city for WrestleMania 42.

The Greater New Orleans Sports Foundation released a statement on the matter, saying, "The Greater New Orleans Sports Foundation and New Orleans & Company are working closely with our friends at TKO to expand our long-standing partnership, which will include UFC 318 on July 19, 2025, Money in the Bank in 2026, and WrestleMania(—)which will move from the currently scheduled 2026 timeframe to a future year."

Hosting WrestleMania 45 would satisfy the latter part of that statement, and mark the third WrestleMania to emanate from New Orleans.

The first two instances were WrestleMania 30 in 2014 and WrestleMania 34 in 2018, and both of those events were held at the New Orleans Saints' Superdome as well.

Next year's WrestleMania 43, which is scheduled for April 2027, will take place in Saudi Arabia, making it the first-ever WrestleMania outside the United States or Canada.

WWE has yet to indicate where WrestleMania 44 in 2028 may be held.

articles.title: Nebraska Cornhuskers fans are dropping serious money on old stadium urinal troughs
articles.summary: Nebraska Cornhuskers are selling vintage porcelain urinal troughs from Memorial Stadium for $3,000 each as part of the stadium's renovation.
articles.body: I'm not sure what the going rate is for a urinal these days. If you told me they run several thousand dollars, I'd believe you, and if you told me you could get away with dropping $150 on one, I'd believe that too. It turns out that urinals that have spent time inside a college football stadium are in demand and even commanding high prices. The Nebraska Cornhuskers are gearing up to renovate Memorial Stadium, and that means getting rid of some of the old features and fixtures and selling them off to fans with some disposable income. UNIVERSITY OF FLORIDA INTENDS TO MOVE FORWARD WITH $1.45 BILLION STADIUM RENOVATION PLANS Of course, there was one piece of memorabilia that caught everyone's attention, and that was the urinal troughs. Because, again, who wouldn't want a urinal trough that has seen a century's worth of game days? The vintage urinals are on sale and commanding a price of $3,000 a piece. Even wilder, The Athletic reports that they've managed to sell seven of the thirty available porcelain urinals, which is — carry the one; switch the numerator and denominator... — $21,000 in urinals. WILT CHAMBERLAIN WARM-UP JACKET BOUGHT FOR $3 AT THRIFT STORE SELLS FOR TENS OF THOUSANDS That's high, but not a bad deal if you're looking for a piece to really pull together the bathroom in your finished basement or sports bar. Hell, I think it would be mighty fine in the living room. What a conversation piece. "Yeah, we got rid of the old coffee table a couple months back and replaced it with this urinal trough from Memorial Stadium. You know, it actually predates light beer by several decades. Rumor has it Richard Nixon may have even used it one time..." *(Guests ooh and aah; one snaps a flash photo) That is some big-brain thinking from the folks at Nebraska because most of us would've just thrown our century-old porcelain urinals in the dump. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP But, as it turns out, as the adage states: one man's trash is another's urine-soaked treasure.

articles.title: South Africa host Australia who battle more than ‘Sandpapergate’ memories
articles.summary: WTC holders South Africa host Australia, who struggled against Bangladesh, in Tests for first time since 2018 scandal.
articles.body:
Australia play their first Test in South Africa since the 2018 ball-tampering scandal when they start a ⁠three-match series in Durban on Friday, with the visitors unlikely to face more than a few heckles over the incident that rocked the sport eight years ago.

The tourists’ efforts to roughen ⁠up the ball using sandpaper to aid reverse swing in Cape Town in March 2018 were caught on camera and led to a major reckoning for the game in Australia, with captain Steve Smith among those banned for their role in the subterfuge.

Al Jazeera Sport takes a closer look at the first Test battle in South Africa since the infamous series.

What is the context for the first return of series since ‘Sandpapergate’

South Africa have played Tests in Australia since ‘Sandpapergate’, and ‌Australia have toured South Africa in the interim for limited-overs internationals.

The scandal has attracted little media focus in South Africa over recent weeks in comparison to the attention devoted to the incident in the Australian press.

After dethroning Australia last year in a thrilling World Test Championship (WTC) final at Lord’s to win a first major title, South Africa are focused on improving their chances of a return to the final at the end of the 2025–27 ⁠WTC cycle.

What shape are South Africa in for the visit of Australia?

The pitch at Kingsmead often proves a fickle track but should offer the spinners a chance to play a leading role in ⁠a change from South Africa’s usually seamer-friendly surfaces.

It is unusual for South Africa’s chances to be largely entrusted to their spin attack, but Simon ⁠Harmer and Keshav Maharaj wreaked havoc in India last November ⁠when they triumphed in their last two Test outings.

Spin was also a key factor for the home side as they beat Australia in the recent One-Day International series.

South Africa may therefore opt to rest frontline attack bowler Kagiso Rabada from ‌the Test as he continues his comeback from a hamstring injury.

South Africa also have a choice to make over their number three batsman, with coach Shukri Conrad having several options including a potential first cap for 30-year-old Marques Ackerman.

How are Australia poised for their South Africa return?

Australia are also in need of a boost after a surprise ⁠home Test defeat by Bangladesh in August in their drawn series , and with an Ashes tour to England starting next June.

Injury to Australia all-rounder Cameron Green opens up a chance at number five for Cooper Connolly, or a fairytale return for ‌34-year-old ‌Nic Maddinson after recovering from cancer.

Australia opener Travis Head has taken to task former Test players turned critics whom he accused on Wednesday of “putting a bullet” through the current team.

Head did not single out any pundit directly, but his strong remarks at a news conference came the day after Matthew Hayden, one-time holder of the record ⁠for the most runs in a Test innings, accused selectors of “promoting the greatest pile of mediocrity that we’ve seen in a generation of cricket”.

The reference, made in a podcast, was about the recall of Maddinson, who has been out of Test cricket for nearly 10 years, but who joined the squad in South Africa after Josh Inglis ‌fractured his finger and Cameron Green suffered a stomach injury.

“I think it’s unfairly judged a fair bit from a group of past players, pretty much that put the bullet through a lot of players, which I think is unfair,” Head said.

“But that’s what they’re paid to do. Some of them need a job, so they go after us, and that’s totally fine.

“This group is strong enough to deal with those sorts of things. That’s how it is. It’s unfortunate sometimes to have some of that feedback from a ⁠generation of players that we have huge respect for, but that’s the caper.”

Why have Australia selectors been accused of disrespecting cricket?

Hayden accused the selectors of “disrespecting first-class cricket”, asserting that batsmen should have an average of 45 runs or more before being considered for Test selection.

Head, however, praised Maddinson’s abilities and the benefits of choosing experienced players for Test cricket despite the 34-year-old ⁠replacement having a first-class average of 37.11.

“We need mature guys that know what they need to be doing,” Head said. “That revolves back to why ⁠we’ve been so good over a period of time, and why Australian ⁠cricket was so good back then in that era, because you’d bring in the Mike Husseys of the world, who are 30, who are tried and tested and know what they need to do.”

Former Australia captain Allan Border suggested that the 32-year-old Head would face his ‌toughest test as an opener against the South African bowling attack and would perhaps be better batting at number five.

“I have laughed at a fair bit of it because if a traditional opening batter had pushed out ‌the ‌same sort of numbers in his first 20 innings, I think he’d be pretty safe and not talked about in the way that it has been talked about,” Head said. “It’s a lot of headline stuff.”

Smith still traumatised by Sandpapergate

In the build-up to the series, Smith has admitted he is still traumatised by “Sandpapergate” – the series he oversaw as captain.

The prolific batter was sent home in disgrace, banned for a year and sacked as captain for his role in the ball-tampering scandal during the third Test in Cape Town eight years ago.

David Warner, considered the ringleader, was suspended for 12 months and stripped of all leadership roles, while Cameron Bancroft was slapped with a nine-month ban.

Smith said he still suffers flashbacks to a traumatic period of his life, haunted by memories of leaving Johannesburg airport, with cameras clicking furiously around him, and a harrowing Sydney news conference on his return when he broke down in tears.

“I’m not a big fan of cameras … I get anxious around cameras to be honest,” he told News Corp.

“That was a traumatic experience in my life, and when I hear the flash of a camera it makes me revisit that in a way.

“The 24-48 hours of being told by James Sutherland [then Cricket Australia chief executive] that I was getting banned for a year. That and going through the airport in Johannesburg getting absolutely mobbed, and then flying back and doing that press conference.

“I still have little flashbacks here and there of it.”

Smith bore the brunt of the scandal that is considered one of Australian sport’s darkest moments, but bounced back emphatically.

He smashed a superb century against England on his return and has gone from strength to strength, with 10,920 Test runs so far at an average of 56.

“It was certainly a difficult period, particularly the initial period a few days after,” he said.

“The mental state I was in was not great. That’s somewhere I’d like not to get to again, but I certainly learned from that and have been able to move forward with my life.

“I’ve tried to kind of erase a lot of 2018 and what happened,” he added.

“I can’t remember a lot about the series. I’ve tried to block most of it out of my memory bank.”

Smith has been back to South Africa for a white-ball series since 2018, but not for a Test, and he is bracing for hostile crowds.

But the 37-year-old is unperturbed, having negotiated multiple Ashes tours to England since 2018, where the Barmy Army abused him relentlessly.

“It’s something I’m kind of used to. I’ve copped a lot at times away from home at different venues across my career and it’s something that I take in my own stride,” he said.

“I use it as motivation to try and go out and do well and try and take a positive from it.”

articles.title: Oilers Checked Into Health Concern Before Making Filip Hallander Trade
articles.summary: Before acquiring Filip Hallander in a deal that sent Spencer Stastney to Pittsburgh, the Edmonton Oilers made sure to look into one specific potential issue:...
articles.body:
Before acquiring Filip Hallander in a deal that sent Spencer Stastney to Pittsburgh, the Edmonton Oilers made sure to look into one specific potential issue: the blood clot that sidelined the forward for a significant chunk of last season.

Back in November 2025, the Penguins announced that Hallander had been diagnosed with a blood clot in his leg, an issue serious enough to keep him out a minimum of three months. He wound up playing only 13 games in the NHL last season. At the time, the 24-year-old remained in Pittsburgh to rehab with the team's medical staff and UPMC rather than travel with the team to Sweden.

Penguins head coach Dan Muse knew it wasn't good. "It's terrible. At the same time, though, when something like this comes up, this goes way beyond hockey. This is about the person," Muse said, adding that the team was "thankful and grateful" medical staff caught the issue quickly enough to begin treatment.

Fast forward to Wednesday's trade, and Hallander is now an Oiler. Edmonton GM Stan Bowman confirmed the club did its homework on the health scare before finalizing the trade, and that early signs point to no long-term effects.

Hallander is expected to join the team in San Jose and practice with his new teammates Friday.

Bowman made clear the interest in Hallander predates the injury entirely and seems to think this trade is worth any potential health risk. "We've been interested in his game since his time in Sweden," Bowman said. "He brings offensive instincts, playmaking ability, work ethic, competitiveness, and pace, and we believe he'll fit perfectly with the way Mike wants our players to play."

The Timing Just Made Sense For the Oilers

"We came into the year with eight defensemen, and we knew that wasn't something we were going to go with all year," he explained. Then, as the season approached, a string of forward injuries created another need for additional depth. Trading a blueliner for a forward became the logical move, even if the injuries the Oilers do have aren't considered long-term.

As for where Hallander fits and if he'll be a regular in the lineup, that much is unclear. The Oilers may take their time with him, even though he's gotten off to a solid start with the Penguins this season. This is still an unproven player, and the Oilers have squeezed out points in their first three games.

"He played a really offensive style when he was in Sweden," Bowman said. "I think it's good to see that he's got that ability to make plays. But in addition, we like the fact that he's a worker and he competes." That suggests he'll be a bottom-six guy, playing alongside the likes of Josh Samanski, Mathieu Joseph, Owen Michaels, Colton Dach, and Trent Frederic.

With the medical concerns apparently behind him, the hope in Edmonton is that Hallander can finally deliver on the potential that first caught the organization's attention years ago.

articles.title: 10-year-old hockey players threatened with suspension by club owner over ‘egregious’ team merch
articles.summary: A threat to suspend 10-year-olds over unauthorized team merch went viral. The N.J. hockey owner explains what happened.
articles.body:
A New Jersey youth hockey dispute that erupted on social media this week began with an email threatening to suspend 10-year-old players over jackets their parents bought without the organization's approval.

But the players were never suspended, according to Bobby Reiss, owner of the Jersey Hitmen and the Ice Vault rink in Wayne, who said Wednesday that all of them attended practice as scheduled.

Reiss told NJ.com the warning was intended to pressure the players' parents into addressing what he considered a violation of the organization's rules.

"Nobody was suspended," Reiss said. "They all practiced last night."

Reiss acknowledged writing in an email to parents that their children would be suspended, but said the threat was meant to get the parents' attention. He added that none of the parents were actually forced to pay royalties at this point.

"Did I write that they would be? Yes, I did," Reiss said. "But that was to get the attention of the mothers."

The controversy began after a group of mothers associated with the Hitmen's 10U major team had custom jackets made using team branding, according to Reiss.

In his email, Reiss said Hitmen logos and trademarks could not be used without permission and that the prohibition was spelled out in team contracts. He wrote that the parents and their children would be suspended until "restitution" was made to the organization in the form of a 15% royalty.

The email quickly spread online and was highlighted by Barstool Sports , which portrayed the dispute as a youth hockey organization suspending 10-year-olds because their mothers made matching jackets. The story subsequently went viral across social media.

Reiss said that characterization left out an important part of the story.

"We had no intent of not letting the kids practice," he said. "That was to get the attention of the parents."

Reiss said the organization employs people who produce team merchandise and argued that parents who independently create products using the Hitmen brand are using the organization's trademarks without permission while taking business away from employees who make apparel for the club.

He also said families agreed to restrictions on the use of Hitmen branding when they signed their contracts.

"All I want people to do is respect the boundaries that you agreed to," Reiss said. "We provide a service, they partake of the service, but within that service, there are restrictions."

Reiss said he selected the 15% royalty because he considered it comparable to licensing fees charged by larger sports organizations.

"I just picked a figure," he said, adding that he believed it was generally in line with licensing fees elsewhere in sports.

Asked why he threatened the ice time of children over a dispute involving their parents, Reiss was candid.

"The only way parents deal is through their kids," he said. "When their actions (cause) potential issues for their children, then they'll deal with the issue at hand."

In his email, Reiss wrote that he did not "relish taking it out on the players" but could not see another immediate way to handle the matter.

When asked whether he considered other options, Reiss said: "There really wasn't any. The only option that you have is ice time."

But Reiss emphasized that no ice time was ultimately taken away.

Reiss explained his decision to threaten suspension.

"That's why I used that terminology: 'I'll suspend your kids,'" he said. "The only way I can get their interest."

Reiss said the underlying dispute remained unresolved because he had not spoken directly with the parents. But he insisted the children would not be punished as it continues.

"The kids will never be affected," Reiss said. "Let me make that perfectly clear."

Reiss said he was frustrated that the dispute became public and argued that the parents should have approached him directly.

"I'm from an era where you resolve these things face to face," Reiss said. "What they did is they took it to the press purposely to make me and the organization look bad."

He acknowledged that the publicity had portrayed him negatively but stood by his position that families cannot use the organization's branding without permission.

"They're now trying to paint me in a bad light, which in a way I'm not going to deny they have," Reiss said. "But I don't really care about that."

Reiss said the organization has allowed families to create certain items in the past when they first sought permission and the Hitmen could not produce the items themselves.

"If I can't do it, that's a different story," he said. "They didn't explore that with me. They never gave me a shot."

It has come to my attention that the Mothers of our 10U major team took upon themselves to design and make jackets that used the Hitmen logos. In all Bandit and Hitmen contracts it VERY specifically says that no one is allowed to use these trademarks. These trademarks are Federally registered and any transgressions over the years have been dealt with by our law firm. All of you know that we have the most comprehensive team apparel of any youth organization in the country. We take great pride in what we produce and are very protective of our rights. When you signed your contracts, we make this very self-evident by incorporating into all contracts.

The parents involved in this were so proud that they took a video which I am sure will circulate, as all things do, on social media. I cannot permit or tolerate these actions. Therefore, the parents on this team and their children are suspended until restitution is made to our organization. Parents who were not involved can continue to practice. Restitution will consist of a 15% Royalty which is common place for the rights to use a company's trademark providing, you get permission, which was not sought out or granted in this case. If the person or persons that initiated this trademark infringement come forward, along with a copy of the bill of sale from the supplier, as well as the payment of the royalty we will allow their players to practice immediately as soon as we have the discussion.

This has been one of the most egregious violations in recent memory of someone taking upon themselves to violate this policy in our contracts. I don't relish taking it out on the players, but I cannot see any other way to deal with this in the immediate time.

articles.title: Wisconsin’s Kyrah Daniels reframes ongoing injury recovery as ‘blessing’
articles.summary: Wisconsin women's basketball guard Kyrah Daniels is not back on the court yet after suffering an injury in the WBIT semifinals in March.
articles.body:
ROSEMONT, Ill. – Wisconsin women's basketball has needed to be patient from a medical standpoint as the Badgers prepare for the 2026-27 season .

Kyrah Daniels – one of Wisconsin 's key returning players – is still recovering from an injury she suffered in the Badgers' WBIT semifinal loss to Columbia on March 30.

"She's getting there," Wisconsin coach Robin Pingeton said at the Big Ten's annual basketball media days. "She's not back on the court yet, but we do expect her to be back relatively soon."

Any missed time from a key player would be an obvious disappointment for the Badgers , but the challenging circumstances have not deterred Daniels from maintaining a positive mindset at this point in the preseason.

"Nobody wants to get hurt, but it's been such a blessing to be able to take a step back and kind of work on the things I need to work on, especially mentally," Daniels said. "I think physically, I also want to get better. But mentally, it's been a really good opportunity to be even a leader, see stuff on the sideline that you don't get to see when you're playing and things like that."

That positivity is not lost upon Pingeton either.

"The ability to reframe 'unfortunate injury' into something that could be really positive and to just continue to help her grow, I think, is really important," Pingeton said. "And I think she's really embraced that."

Daniels is coming off a 2025-26 season where she averaged 12.4 points, 5.1 rebounds, 2.6 assists and 1.2 steals in 30.4 minutes per game. She is the top returning player in each of those categories in 2026-27.

While Pingeton has seen Daniels "chomping at the bit" to return to the court, the second-year UW coach has preached patience with her recovery.

"With an injury like that, you want to be really cautious that you don't push the limits too quickly," Pingeton said. "And first and foremost, we want her to be healthy, and then we want her to be back on the court. … I think our doctors, our trainers have done a phenomenal job with her."

Wisconsin has a nonconference schedule that could nicely accommodate that patience, too, playing only two power-conference teams before Big Ten play begins. (Those power-conference matchups against Auburn and Syracuse are part of a holiday tournament in Puerto Rico.)

The injury recovery is just one aspect of an eventful offseason for Daniels ahead of her fourth season of college basketball. Daniels briefly entered the transfer portal after the 2025-26 season before withdrawing and returning to the Badgers.

It was one of many offseason wins for Pingeton and the Badgers. The additions of NEC player of the year Kadidia Toure, SoCon player of the year Caia Elisaldez and ex-Iowa players Addie Deal and Teagan Mallegni were some of the others.

"We're in a crazy time of college sports right now, and so it's so interesting – all the pulls and opinions and pressures," Daniels said, looking back at her entry and withdrawal from the portal. "But I think the biggest thing is the clarity of how exciting it is to be a part of Wisconsin women's basketball and what we're building."

She credited Pingeton for her willingness to "have hard conversations" and "dig in and get to the root of things."

"I think that is a testament to who Coach P is and the leader that she is that she would be willing to have a really good, honest conversation with me about what it looks like," Daniels said.

Pingeton's conversations in the spring – easy and hard, whether it be with Daniels or others – have preceded optimism in the fall for what the Badgers can accomplish in 2026-27.

"We've got to stay healthy – get healthy and stay healthy," Pingeton said. "But I'm really excited about our depth. I think we've got a lot of versatility, and I think we've got a lot of buy-in in regards to continuing to move the needle for this program."

articles.title: Patriots quarterback Drake Maye says he's 'a little bit skeptical' about the moon landing
articles.summary: Patriots quarterback and newly crowned AFC player of the week Drake Maye said this week that he's "a little bit skeptical" that humans landed on the moon.
articles.body:
After a slow start to the season , the New England quarterback seemed to return to his almost-MVP form from a year ago (he finished second in voting to the Rams' Matthew Stafford ) on Sunday during a 29-26 win over the previously unbeaten Buffalo Bills.

On Wednesday, Maye was announced as the AFC offensive player of the week for his efforts in that game, which included completing 22 of 37 passes for 269 yards with three touchdowns and one interception and rushing for 54 yards in eight attempts.

With Maye-mania surely back on track in New England, there was probably no better time for the third-year quarterback to casually drop that he kinda, sorta, maybe, possibly isn't quite sure moon landings have ever actually happened.

During an appearance Monday on WEEI-FM (93.7) in Boston, Maye was asked by a caller, "What wild conspiracy theory out there do you actually kind of secretly believe in?"

Maye asked for a moment to think — "let me try not to get too controversial," he said — before revealing his answer.

"I don't know about the moon, you know?" Maye said. "I'm not really sure 200% if we went there or not. I wouldn't say I'm leaning one way or the other. I just know I'm a little bit skeptical."

Maye spent three years at North Carolina, including two as the Tar Heels' starting quarterback. In 2022, he set a school record with 4,321 passing yards, tied another with 38 passing touchdowns and was named the Atlantic Coast Conference player of the year.

During his time at Chapel Hill, Maye said during the radio interview earlier this week, he took a class on conspiracy theories.

"They studied Hitler being alive and 'are birds real?' — some of the classic ones that you hear about," Maye explained.

Asked to elaborate on the birds one, Maye said there are some who believe birds are actually instruments of the government used to spy on us — "or something along the lines of that," he said.

Maye isn't the only athlete who has expressed moon-landing doubt. In 2018, Stephen Curry said he didn't think humans had ever been there, although two days later the Golden State Warriors superstar said that he was kidding .

Former NASCAR and IndyCar driver Danica Patrick reportedly posted one such theory on her Instagram Stories in 2024 and wrote that she believes it.

"I don't care if you think I'm crazy," she wrote. "I already know I am."

Earlier this year, Boston Celtics guard Derrick White described himself as a "non-moon landing guy." Also, two-time major golf champion Bryson DeChambeau said that while it's likely that moon landings have happened, some of the footage we've been shown might have been fake.

This story originally appeared in Los Angeles Times .

articles.title: Memphis Grizzlies center Zach Edey making preseason debut vs Magic
