Memphis Grizzlies center Zach Edey will play against the Orlando Magic on Oct. 7, coach Tuomas Iisalo said.

Edey, drafted No. 9 overall in 2024, has had two ankle procedures since joining the NBA. His most recent came after playing just 15 games last season.

The Grizzlies have said that Edey has been fully cleared, but they have been cautiously monitoring him. Playing in the regular-season opener on Oct. 21 has been the priority for Edey, and the Grizzlies were pleased with his progress.

"This was pretty much the best-case scenario that we had planned, and there was nothing that prevented us from going through," Iisalo said.

The Grizzlies will be conservative with Edey's minutes, Iisalo said.

As for the rest of the team, the starters will see gradual increases in minutes played. Every player stayed under 20 minutes in the preseason opener. Ty Jerome and Quinten Post played in only the first half before sitting out the second half of the Oct. 5 win over the Atlanta Hawks.

articles.title: C.J. Stroud was mic'd up in the Texans game vs. the Cowboys. He explains why and his passion
articles.summary: C.J. Stroud usually says no to be mic'd up but he did this week against the Cowboys. He explains his passion after a TD pass to Nico Collins.
articles.body:
A video of a mic'd up C.J. Stroud from Sunday's game versus the Dallas Cowboys made the rounds this week on social media as it showcased the Houston Texans quarterback's on-field passion.

Stroud, who is typically more stoic in public settings, told the media Wednesday that spirit in the video wasn't just for the cameras but something that is intrinsic in his character as a football player.

"I've always been passionate," Stroud said. "I've always loved playing this game. This game has truly done incredible things for me and my family, and I believe God has put a certain fire in me to have an excitement about playing each play."

The video started with Stroud throwing one of his two touchdowns to wide receiver Nico Collins before going into the immediate aftermath of the score: Stroud hyping himself up after the play, doing his handshake with Collins and then the aftermath on the sideline.

Stroud said he typically says no to mic'd up situations because of how he gets on the field but he believes his teammates love to see him when he's at that level.

"We could be playing in Sunnyside, I would be excited to play this game. I really love this game," Stroud said.

Despite the 0-4 record for the Texans, Stroud has been arguably the best player on the Texans offense through the first four games of the season. He threw for over 300 yards for the second time this year in the 34-30 loss to the Cowboys, finding Collins for two touchdowns.

But Stroud said that when he looks at himself in the mirror, he's reflecting not on what he did well but on the things he can do better.

"I feel the rhythm," Stroud said. "I feel like I'm putting the ball where I need to put it. But also you know I just want to be better on third down and you know in the red zone."

articles.title: Eagles vs. Jaguars prediction, odds, pick for Week 5 NFL London Game
articles.summary: The Jacksonville Jaguars (3-1) are favored over the Philadelphia Eagles (2-2) in London, and the number tells the story: Philadelphia is a road underdog by a...
articles.body:
The Jacksonville Jaguars (3-1) are favored over the Philadelphia Eagles (2-2) in London, and the number tells the story: Philadelphia is a road underdog by as many as 7 points, a spot the Eagles haven't been in for years. A depleted offense and a Jaguars defense that has allowed just 53 points all season make Jacksonville the clear side.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Philadelphia's list reads like a roster of its best players. Running back Saquon Barkley (hamstring) is likely out and considered week-to-week after leaving the Rams loss after four snaps. Tank Bigsby (core muscle) is headed to injured reserve , leaving Will Shipley as the last healthy running back on the active roster.

The offensive line took another hit when Lane Johnson announced his retirement this week . Wide receiver DeVonta Smith and tight end Dallas Goedert remain questionable, as do linebacker Zack Baun, edge rusher Jonathan Greenard and cornerback Quinyon Mitchell.

Jacksonville is in better shape but has some concerns in the secondary. Safeties Eric Murray (concussion) and Caleb Ransaw (knee) are questionable after leaving Sunday's win over Cincinnati, and cornerback Montaric Brown missed that game.

The Eagles have not covered the spread yet this season, and three of their four games have gone over the total. Jacksonville is 3-1 against the spread, with only one of its four games going over.

The Jaguars have covered 14 of their last 21 games against the spread and won 15 of their last 21 straight up.

Philadelphia's offense is the main problem. It went 0-for-12 on third down against the Rams, the most third-down attempts without a conversion by the franchise since at least 1991. Jalen Hurts faced pressure on 57.6% of his dropbacks, and the Eagles have yet to top 24 points in a game while averaging 4.2 yards per carry.

Jacksonville's defense is built to exploit that. The Jaguars have six interceptions through four games, tied for the NFL lead entering Monday, and their defense ranked second in red-zone success rate allowed (20%) before Sunday. They blitz on third-and-long only 21.1% of the time, but the Rams' blueprint of heavy pressure on third down worked.

The Eagles' best hope is a defense that held a 20-10 lead on the Rams until the final four minutes, plus Jacksonville's 13 penalties in the Bengals win. Even so, they travel late, arriving in London less than 36 hours before kickoff.

Jacksonville has the better defense, a healthier roster and an Eagles offense that is struggling to move the chains. Without Barkley, Bigsby and Johnson, Philadelphia has little to lean on against a unit that rarely gives up points.

The Eagles' defense can keep it close, but the margin should favor Jacksonville late. The line sits close to a key number, so shop for the best price.

Take the Jaguars to win and cover, with the under also appealing at 42.5.

With Barkley likely out and Tank Bigsby going on injured reserve, the Eagles have two running backs on the roster: Will Shipley and Dameon Pierce, who was called up from the practice squad on Wednesday. They also still have Carson Steele and Jaydon Blue on the practice squad.

Smith was seen stretching on the sideline as the rest of the team warmed up together. Seems like he'll miss this game but maybe he has a chance to return in Week 6? We'll see.

Kendall's knee injury is a new development. If he can't play, the Eagles will have to go with their third different starting center through five games this season. Willie Lampkin could get the nod at the pivot with … Fred Johnson? Jake Majors? Micah Morris? … at left guard. Not exactly ideal.

Greenard suffered an ankle injury in Week 4. He's reportedly " day-to-day ," which is typically less serious than "week-to-week." We'll see if he's able to practice at all on Thursday. If not, he'll probably miss Sunday. But he might then be able to return in Week 6.

Campbell is listed with a knee injury. If the second-year linebacker can't suit up, look for Jeremiah Trotter Jr. to start in his place. There have been calls for the Eagles to bench Campbell in favor of Trot Jr. When asked about Trot Jr. earlier this week, Fangio said he "played very well." Then asked if Trot Jr. warrants more playing time, Fangio said: "Possibly, yeah."

Epps could miss a second straight game. If that's the case, look for Michael Carter II to play safety in the Eagles' nickel packages next to Andrew Mukuba. Cooper DeJean is still starting at safety in Philly's base defense. Kenny Moore II will provide depth on the back end as he gets more acclimated to playing a new position.

Brown is on track to miss his third game in a row. If he's not ready to play in Week 6, the Eagles will have wasted his roster spot when they could've just put him on IR to miss four games. If Brown and Smith both don't play, the Eagles will roll with the following five receivers: Dontayvion Wicks, Darius Cooper, Makai Lemon, Britain Covey, and Elijah Moore.

Mitchell suffered a knee injury in Week 4 that prevented him from returning to the game after he left. Seems like he might be able to suit up this week. Or next week at the latest. If not, it'll be seasoned veteran Jonathan Jones starting in his place.

Baun miss Week 4 while in the concussion protocol. That he's progressed to the point where he can be limited in practice is a good sign for his chances of playing this weekend. It could be Baun and Trot Jr. starting at off-ball linebacker. Big boost for the Eagles' defense to get Baun back.

If so, the Eagles could have four tight ends active for Sunday: Goedert, Johnny Mundt, Zach Ertz, and E.J. Jenkins. Will be interesting to see how that snap count plays out.

Fred Johnson returned to practice after missing the Eagles' last two games. articles.title: Max Verstappen on life after Christian Horner: “It is less stressful”
articles.summary: Max Verstappen has praised the calmer atmosphere under Laurent Mekies
articles.body:
Max Verstappen has admitted that he doesn't miss the friction that was created when Christian Horner was leading the Red Bull Formula 1 team. Speaking to the Press Association , the four-time champion admitted that the team is less stressful now his former boss has left the championship.

Conflict sells. Arguments between and within teams create plots that shape the likes of Drive to Survive and headlines across the globe. But from a driver's point of view, they are uninterested in complicating what should be a professional environment purely focused on winning the next race.

"To be honest, I like to see that people get on," he said when asked about Horner. "It is not nice when you constantly have tension between people."

He added: "Of course, from the outside, people like it, but honestly between the teams, it is better when you have just a friendly relationship."

With Red Bull under the control of Frenchman Laurent Mekies and with one win now under its belt this season, the Dutchman is enjoying his life at Milton Keynes.

"It is not as spicy, but I obviously quite like how things are going at the moment, with everyone's behaviour, let's put it like that."

The driver also gave a commonsensical reason as to why this is his preference: less conflict means fewer distractions.

"It is less stressful. We are all leading a stressful life and, when you can take a bit of stress out of it at times, it is good."

Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing, Laurent Mekies, Red Bull Racing Team Principal

The team removed Horner from its ranks last year after a period of controversy and differing results. He was eventually replaced by Mekies, who took on his role of team principal and CEO after a solid period at its sister team Racing Bulls .

Verstappen leaves the door open to Horner Verstappen, wanting to continue his luck in Singapore this weekend after a successful Sunday in Malaysia, was asked about the possibility of Horner returning to the paddock.

"He has shown he did a good job. Of course, people spread a lot of rumours, and I don't know how much of that is true. I don't want to sound rude, but it is also not my problem or concern. He wants to come back, and if there is a good opportunity, I am sure he will do it, but I don't know where that is going to be."

Formula 1 can keep its drama. Verstappen would simply prefer fewer people bringing it into the office.

articles.title: Texans HC DeMeco Ryans calls audible, takes over play-calling duties vs. Titans
articles.summary: While there might not be many changes made to the Houston Texans' staff entering Sunday's game against the Tennessee Titans, there's at least one big one for...
articles.body:
While there might not be many changes made to the Houston Texans' staff entering Sunday's game against the Tennessee Titans , there's at least one big one for DeMeco Ryans .

The Texans head coach announced Wednesday during his press conference that he would be taking over defensive play-calling duties for the first time in over a year.

When hired back in 2023, Ryans served as the primary play-caller for two-plus seasons. Then, after an 0-3 start last season, he handed the duties over to defensive coordinator Matt Burke, which led to a team turnaround and the league's No. 1 scoring unit.

"If guys are saying communication is not right, then that ultimately it falls on me," Ryans said. "So I'm going to get it fixed. It's no slight on Coach Burke. He's done an outstanding job. I just want to make sure I streamline communication in the best way possible so that isn't the theme when I stand up here and see you guys."

Credit, Ryans is addressing the biggest problem for the team so far this season. Houston's offense, despite its flaws, has scored 30 or more points twice and led within the final minute of two games. Ultimately, the defense is what let down the offense, resulting in an 0-4 start instead of a 2-2 or even 3-1 record.

Entering Sunday's AFC South matchup against the Titans, Houston ranks 20th in total yards allowed per game and 26th in points allowed. They also have only forced three turnovers, all of which came in Week 3's road loss to Indianapolis. And despite ranking top three in sacks with 14, Houston's pressure rate is outside the top 10.

To some, the decision could be viewed as a demotion for the fourth-year defensive coordinator. After all, Burke was in the running for several head coaching openings last season.

Still, the Texans are trying to make history and avoid it at the same time. The only way to do that is to shake up the until somethng clicks.

"I'm not in this role to please a lot of people's opinion. I have to do what's best for this team and make sure I'm leading in that way," Ryans said. "Unfortunately, everybody isn't happy when you make changes, when you make decisions from my chair, everybody isn't happy. That's okay, because I know everything that I try to do and strive to do is for the men in that locker room to give those guys as best chance as possible to go out and win our first football game."

Kickoff is scheduled for Noon on CBS from Nissan Stadium.

articles.title: Carroll football's suspension upheld by LHSAA executive committee
articles.summary: An LHSAA official confirmed to the Monroe News-Star that the executive committee upheld Carroll's suspension Wednesday.
articles.body:
MONROE — The LHSAA executive committee unanimously upheld Carroll High School football's rest-of-season suspension on Wednesday, Oct. 7, an LHSAA official confirmed to the Monroe News-Star.

The Bulldogs, who finished with a 2-2 record, were suspended by the LHSAA's Sportsmanship Committee for the remainder of the 2025-26 season following a postgame altercation after their 14-6 loss at Assumption. The Mustangs were fined $500 and will not host any more home games for the rest of the season.

"No members of the Sportsmanship Committee participated as voting members in the Executive Committee's appeal decision," the LHSAA wrote in a statement.

Carroll filed an appeal of its suspension with the LHSAA last Thursday. State senator and Bulldogs graduate Katrina Jackson-Andrews said in an interview with the News-Star the punishment Carroll received was a "disproportionate" response to what happened after the Carroll-Assumption game.

"My heart goes out to the seniors who are facing their season ending," Jackson-Andrews said regarding the suspension.

(This story will be updated with more information.)

articles.title: “All Time Playoff Choker” – Fans Throw Shade at Chris Sale for Dismal Postseason Record As Dodgers Legend Clayton Kershaw Also Catches Strays
articles.summary: After giving up two crucial home runs in NLDS Game 3, Atlanta Braves ace Chris Sale is receiving the same reception Clayton Kershaw faced for most of his car...
articles.body:
After giving up two crucial home runs in NLDS Game 3, Atlanta Braves ace Chris Sale is receiving the same reception Clayton Kershaw faced for most of his career. The Braves lost 3-1 to the Dodgers on Tuesday, with Kike Hernández and Freddie Freeman taking the southpaw deep in the fourth inning.

Kershaw, who failed to live up to postseason expectations many times for the Dodgers despite his status as a legend for the franchise, was used to such criticism. Like Kershaw, Sale is a former Cy Young winner who has had postseason struggles and therefore is enduring a similar reception on social media. In nine postseason starts, Sale holds a 6.52 career ERA and a 1-4 record.

"He's up there with Kershaw for all time playoff choker ✌️✌️✌️✌️✌️," one fan wrote.

Sale and Kershaw, a three-time Cy Young winner, are both known for their dominance in the regular season. However, when the calendar turns to October, they have both struggled at times for their teams.

Including his two relief appearances in the Dodgers' 2025 postseason run, Kershaw's career postseason line stands at 13-13 with a 4.62 ERA and 213 strikeouts over 196.2 innings. He had a 2.53 ERA and 223 wins in the regular season in his 18-season career.

On the other hand, after Tuesday's game, Sale has a 1-4 record with an ERA of 5.79 and 66 strikeouts in 13 postseason appearances (starts and relief) in his career. He has a 2.95 ERA in 16 seasons.

Chris Sale Regrets One Bad Pitch in NLDS Game 3 Loss

Chris Sale started strongly in NLDS Game 3 against the Dodgers, striking out each of the first six batters he faced. However, the Dodgers exhausted him with long at-bats, and the pressure finally got to the southpaw in the fourth inning.

Sale first gave up a two-run home run to Dodgers utility man Kike Hernández, followed by Freddie Freeman hitting a 399-foot solo home run to extend the Dodgers' lead to 3-0. In a game where Dodgers ace Yoshinobu Yamamoto pitched seven strong innings, allowing just one run, there was really no room for Sale to allow two home runs.

After the 3-1 loss, Sale regretted the pitch Hernández hit for the two-run homer.

"Really only one pitch I'd take back from that whole entire outing," Sale said . "This is a game of adjustments. They seemed like they made the adjustment. They were battling, but again, really just one swing changed the whole trajectory of that game."

Sale went five innings, allowing three runs on seven hits while striking out seven. Braves manager Walt Weiss also said the Dodgers did a great job adjusting to Sale and grinding him out during their respective at-bats.

The loss on Tuesday has put Atlanta on the brink of postseason elimination in the NLDS.

articles.title: Atlanta Dream building on playoff momentum with move to State Farm Arena
articles.summary: The Atlanta Dream announced a multi-year deal to move to State Farm Arena in 2027, significantly increasing venue capacity.
articles.body:
The Atlanta Dream are chasing a championship this postseason, but the organization is already making moves aimed at its future.

This week, the Dream announced a multi-year agreement to make State Farm Arena their permanent home beginning in 2027, moving from Gateway Center Arena in College Park.

For Morgan Shaw Parker, the president of the Atlanta Dream, the move is a sign of just how far the franchise has come.

"Never in a million years did I think we would be here that quickly, but it just shows the growth, the demand," Shaw Parker told Channel 2's Karyn Greer in an exclusive interview.

The move represents a dramatic increase in capacity, from roughly 3,200 seats in College Park to more than 17,000 seats downtown, giving more fans a chance to watch one of the WNBA's fastest-growing teams.

Shaw Parker was quick to credit Gateway Center Arena and the City of College Park for helping the franchise grow.

"I can't say enough about the Gateway Arena team, the City of College Park for embracing us. We wouldn't be where we are today without that," she said.

The expansion comes as interest in the Dream continues to rise, fueled by a talented roster that includes stars such as Rhyne Howard, Alyssa Gray, Brionna Jones and rookie sensation Angel Reese.

"There's no way that we get Angel Reese if we weren't doing something right on the court," Shaw Parker said. "Angel chose us."

The franchise says its mission extends beyond winning games.

The Atlanta Dream's name was inspired by Dr. Martin Luther King Jr.'s "I Have a Dream" speech, and Shaw Parker says the organization remains committed to empowering women and lifting underrepresented voices.

"This organization was named by the city of Atlanta 19 years ago after Martin Luther King Jr.'s speech," Shaw Parker said. "If the city names you after something that strong, the 'I Have a Dream' speech, you've got to live by those words."

Shaw Parker also credited the team's ownership group, including Larry Gottesdiener, Suzanne Abair and former Dream player Renee Montgomery, with helping transform the franchise and fuel its growth.

The Dream's future may be bright, but the focus right now is on the court.

Atlanta entered Game 2 of its semifinal series against the New York Liberty with a 1-0 lead in the best-of-five matchup.

Team officials hope the combination of playoff success, star power and a future in State Farm Arena will help propel the franchise to new heights.

articles.title: Three changes Michigan State football should consider making
articles.summary: Take a look at three changes Michigan State football should consider making to get the 2026 season back on track.
articles.body:
Michigan State football has hit a crossroad in 2026, the first year of the Pat Fitzgerald era in East Lansing. With the Spartans sitting at 2-3 (0-2 B1G), and suffering their third straight loss, changes are going to have to be made.

The Spartans season is riding on this weekend's matchup with Illinois, with MSU desperately needing a win to get the train back on the tracks.

On Monday, Fitzgerald spoke on some of the things that Michigan State needs to do in order to right the ship in 2026 . Issuing challenges to his players and coaching staff, Fitzgerald has made it known that this program is going to continue to fight this season.

If the Spartans are going to see a change in trends this season, here are three changes the team should consider making:

Could the Joe Rossi era in East Lansing be coming to an end? I think so, and it feels like the writing is on the wall. In all honesty, it was worth bringing Rossi back in 2026, giving him a fresh start, while working to retain several key players including Jordan Hall. Unfortunately, things look the same as they have for the past two seasons, and it feels like it is time for the Spartans to make a move here.

Bringing Bullough back to the program was a big move for Fitzgerald, and it felt like it was a move that was going to lead to the former Spartan linebacker taking over as the team's defensive coordinator at some point in time. It may be a touch earlier than expected, but it feels like that time is now.

Let Bullough control the reigns for the rest of 2026, getting his feet wet and getting the beginner mistakes out of the way, and have him ready to go and take the full reigns of controlling the defense in 2027.

It is no secret, the Michigan State wide receiver room might be the worst unit in the Big Ten. The Spartans are struggling to get any separation in the passing game, are struggling with drops, and just have no cohesiveness to the unit.

Obviously, new guys can't be brought in midseason to totally rectify the problem, but what is stopping the MSU coaching staff from using some of their young guys more in the receiving game? The Spartans have redshirt freshman Braylon Collier, Charles Taplin and Bryson Williams, who have loooked strong in minimal snaps, while also having former 4-star Samson Gash, who deserves a strong look.

Right now, it feels like there is nothing to lose, meaning the Spartans should definitely add in some youth to the wide receiver spot.

OF NOTE: This feels like a last gasp effort from Courtney Hawkins to stay in his position as the wide receivers coach following the season.

I, for one, am not ready to totally call for Alessio Milivojevic to lose his job, but we are getting dangerously close to the point of asking when it is time to see more of Kayd Coffman or Leo Hannan.

Coffman got mop up duty in Madison, and showed some athleticism. It may be worth giving Coffman a look in some of the Cam Fancher packages, now that Fancher is down with an injur, and potentially see if there is some spark in the true freshman.

As of now, this is still Milivojevic's job, but another poor performance against Illinois and the chatter should shift towards seeing what the MSU backups have to offer.

articles.title: Greg Rusedski reacts to Daniil Medvedev ‘mocking’ Novak Djokovic in Beijing before disqualification
articles.summary: Daniil Medvedev mocking Novak Djokovic in their China Open match was the worst thing he could have done, according to Greg Rusedski. The former British...
articles.body:
Daniil Medvedev mocking Novak Djokovic in their China Open match was the worst thing he could have done, according to Greg Rusedski.

The former British number one has shared that verdict after the dust has settled on the semifinal clash, which Djokovic won. But he emerged victorious only after Medvedev was disqualified for hitting a spectator with a ball. The Serbian was, however, leading the Russian 7-5, 5-3 at the time of the default.

Shortly after, Djokovic won the China Open title , although his final against Alex de Minaur was also cut short. He led the Australian 7-6(7-3), 0-1 before De Minaur was forced to retire because of injury.

Former ATP player Rusedski has, however, circled back to the controversy of the Djokovic versus Medvedev tie at the China Open , during which the Russian was spotted apparently mocking the Serbian's physical struggles in Beijing. He claims that was a mistake by Medvedev.

Daniil Medvedev told he made a mistake by mocking Novak Djokovic

Sharing his take on Medvedev's disqualification, Rusedski said on the Off Court With Greg Rusedski podcast : "It is game over, it's unfortunate, it was unintentional, these things happen. He will be bitterly disappointed, because it wasn't intentional, he was about to lose the match, he played a great match. You've got to be very careful where you throw your racket and where you hit the tennis ball, it can be unintentional, but it's an automatic [disqualification], the chair umpire did the right thing, and it was just terribly unfortunate for Daniil Medvedev."

Discussing the rules being there for a reason, he noted: "You can't [do that]. You hit the guy in the eye with a tennis ball… Thomas Johansson, the Australian Open champion, got hit in the eye when he was playing a match and he was out for months on end. The eyes are important, so we want to keep a safe environment for the fan. Sometimes we have to control our anger, these things happen, and he's quite an emotional player, he can lose it. He was mocking Djokovic during that match as well, pretending that he was having breathing problems. He's a unique character, Daniil Medvedev, he's good for the game, and this experience I think he's not going to do that again, it was just an accident and bad luck as well."

And commenting on Medvedev seemingly mocking Djokovic, Rusedski said: "I don't think he was [impressed]. The worst thing you can do is mock Novak. Because when you do that, he actually plays better. You want to keep your mouth shut, you want to play tennis, and you don't want to insult the great champion, because he looks for something a bit more to motivate him, and that's what Daniil gave him. So I think he made a tactical mistake and I think you can't do that to our champions. It's great for our entertainment value, but in respect, if you want to beat Novak Djokovic, you've got to make sure you don't give him extra ammunition."

The match between the experienced duo was full of drama, with China Open fans treated to quite the spectacle on the court. And it was the Serbian who prevailed en route to a 102nd career title. Both players now move on to the ATP Masters 1000 Shanghai, where they could meet in the final after the draw was confirmed.

Djokovic will play the winner of Hubert Hurkacz versus James Duckworth in his opening match, while Medvedev will meet either Martin Landaluce or Jan-Lennard Struff. Both players have received byes in round one in Shanghai, where the Serbian is the 10th seed and the Russian is the fifth.

articles.title: Predicting Ravens’ offensive line depth chart after acquiring Cam Jurgens

Cam Jurgens' arrival gives the Baltimore Ravens an experienced center and a path to move first-round pick Vega Ioane back to his natural position at right guard.

The two-time Pro Bowler is expected to take over at center in Week 6 against Cleveland, provided he clears concussion protocol. That would restore both players to their customary NFL assignments while giving Baltimore more flexibility across an offensive line disrupted by injuries. The projected starting five would feature Ronnie Stanley at left tackle, John Simpson at left guard, Jurgens at center, Ioane at right guard, and Roger Rosengarten at right tackle. Stanley's health remains a significant consideration, while Andrew Vorhees and Emery Jones Jr. provide options inside.

Projected offensive line once Jurgens is available

This projection incorporates Jurgens and returns Ioane to guard. Baltimore's existing depth chart lists Vinson behind both tackles and Vorhees and Jones among its guard options. Ioane's recent work at center gives the Ravens another contingency there.

Baltimore acquired Jurgens after injuries depleted its center depth. Danny Pinter, Jovaughn Gwyn and Ethan Pocic landed on injured reserve, forcing the Ravens to move Ioane inside. Jurgens offers a longer-term solution once he is cleared to play. Philadelphia had moved Jurgens to left guard this season, with Drew Kendall taking over at center after Landon Dickerson's injury. Baltimore's plan returns Jurgens to the position where he earned his two Pro Bowl selections.

His immediate work will involve learning the offense's protection calls and establishing timing with his quarterback and guards.

Ioane began the season as Baltimore's starting right guard before the center injuries forced a change. Jurgens' arrival allows the rookie to resume that assignment.

Ioane handled his first start at center against Tennessee, but returning to guard would give him a more consistent role alongside Rosengarten. His experience at center also remains valuable if Baltimore needs another replacement.

Until Jurgens is available, Ioane remains the logical option to continue snapping the ball.

Andrew Vorhees remains important to the interior.

Vorhees filled the right guard opening created by Ioane's move to center. He left the Tennessee game with a foot injury and did not practice Wednesday. Returning Ioane to guard would move Vorhees into a reserve role.

The trade lets Baltimore rebuild its depth without requiring every available interior lineman to start.

Emery Jones Jr. provides another guard option.

Jones replaced Vorhees against Tennessee and remains part of Baltimore's immediate contingency plan. If Vorhees cannot play while Ioane continues at center, Jones could start at right guard.

Once Jurgens joins the lineup, Jones would remain a reserve guard in the projected configuration.

Ronnie Stanley's health remains a separate concern

Stanley did not practice Wednesday, with rest, toe, and ankle designations on the injury report. His availability remains central to Baltimore's left-side protection.

Vinson is the listed reserve behind Stanley and Rosengarten. Adding Jurgens strengthens the middle of the line, but the Ravens still need healthy tackles and dependable edge depth.

articles.title: Justin Jefferson hopes to play Sunday vs. Saints, fired up by Beckham addition
articles.summary: As expected, Jefferson wants to play in his home state of Louisiana this weekend.
articles.body:
If Justin Jefferson gets his wish, he'll be playing this Sunday when the Vikings take on the Saints at the Superdome in New Orleans, which sits about 30 minutes away from his hometown of St. Rose, Louisiana.

Jefferson exited the Vikings' Week 3 game in Tampa with a sprained ankle, then sat out this past weekend's win over the Dolphins in Minneapolis. He was able to practice in a limited capacity on Wednesday, which is a good sign for his chances of playing this week.

It'll all depend on how his ankle feels over the course of the next few days, but Jefferson said he feels "real good" and is planning on playing this week if everything checks out.

"Hopefully so," he said. "That's definitely the plan. Being back at home in Louisiana is definitely something that I want to do. The plan is for me to play, but who knows?"

"Just taking it day by day," he added. "Ankles are a little bit tricky, so you just gotta continue to stay in the treatment room and making sure that it feels the best that it feels every single day. Coming into this building every day at least feeling a little better than it did before. Getting out there today definitely felt good."

The Vikings have a bye week after this game. They're 4-0. Those are a couple theoretical reasons to lean towards sitting Jefferson against the Saints if he's anything less than 100 percent.

At the same time, he's their superstar and the face of their franchise. His happiness matters. Jefferson desperately wants to play in front of a packed Superdome for the first time in his career. The only previous time he's played in New Orleans came during his rookie season in 2020, when a very limited number of fans were allowed because of the pandemic. In 2022, the Vikings' road game against the Saints was played in London.

"I've definitely been fiending for it, for sure," Jefferson said. "It's definitely been a long time coming. Being back at home with my friends and family being able to watch. LSU fans, the fans that have been watching me for a long period of time. Definitely got a lot of people tuned in to that game, and hopefully I'll play and be able to give them a show."

Jefferson confirmed that he was injured on his second catch of the Vikings' first drive against the Buccaneers, a screen pass in which "four or five" players tackled him, including 350-pound defensive tackle Vita Vea.

"Felt a little tweak," Jefferson said. "Tried to come into the game, tape it up, but I felt a little bit of weakness. Went to the back and looked at the X-rays, it was all good. It was just all about making it feel better, getting the soreness out, the swelling out after the game. But it feels good now, and hopefully Sunday, being able to rock and roll."

Jefferson understands that the bye week is coming up. He also hates missing football games, whenever they are.

"I want to be out there," he said. "That's the main thing. I hate missing games. I hated missing last week; I wanted to be out there last week. Especially at home. I never want to miss any time. It's been a little tough, they've been holding me back a little bit, just not trying to force anything."

Wednesday's news that the Vikings are signing free agent wide receiver Odell Beckham Jr. to their practice squad was exciting to a lot of people, including Kevin O'Connell — but Jefferson is probably at the top of that list.

Beckham and Jefferson have been close for a long time. Beckham overlapped with both of Jefferson's older brothers, Jordan and Rickey, during his time at LSU from 2011-13. Justin, of course, went on to star at LSU in 2018 and '19 before emerging as an NFL superstar and breaking a number of Beckham's early-career records.

"It's definitely cool," Jefferson said. "All of the years that I've watched him play and looked up to his game his play style, on and off the field, how he carried himself as a superstar in the league. We've been brothers for a very long time. The connection has always been there. We've always talked about this moment, one day being able to play with each other. For it to actually be here is definitely crazy. He called me last night to tell me he was coming down. The excitement that we shared together, it was definitely a cool moment."

Jefferson said he's taken a lot of inspiration from watching Beckham play. Beckham joked that he picked jersey No. 9 with the Vikings because "Justin got half his game from me." The two had an older brother-younger brother relationship for a long time that has developed into a friendship as peers over time.

"I've always been a fan of his game," Jefferson said. "He always treated me like a little brother, ever since he was at LSU. Obviously him being in the league and seeing what I was doing at LSU kind of sparked the relationship even more. I modeled my game after him in certain areas — the way he runs his routes, the wiggle at the top of his routes. There's bits and pieces that I took from his game. … To see him out there (at practice) today was a cool moment."

articles.title: Cleveland Guardians stay alive in ALDS, deny White Sox clinch at home
articles.summary: Kyle Teel's early double gave Chicago the lead, but Cleveland's 11-hit explosion in ALDS Game 3 denied the White Sox a series-clinching moment.
articles.body: The Chicago White Sox last clinched a postseason series at home when Jiggs Donahue and George Davis helped the South Siders defeat the Chicago Cubs in Game 6 of the 1906 World Series. More than a century later, the White Sox came up short Thursday in their bid to clinch a spot in the American League Championship Series on their home field, falling to the Cleveland Guardians 7-3 in Game 3. The Guardians haven't made it to what is effectively the MLB's playoffs semifinals since 2005. The White Sox entered the potential ALDS-clinching game with a 2-0 series lead and struck first when catcher Kyle Teel doubled to right field, driving in the game’s first run. WHITE SOX RIDE ANOTHER DRAMATIC COMEBACK WIN TO BEAT GUARDIANS AND TAKE COMMANDING 2-0 ALDS LEAD The Guardians recorded two triples in a postseason game for the first time in franchise history. They became the first major league team to accomplish the feat since the Los Angeles Dodgers in Game 1 of the 2024 World Series. Adell, Ramírez, Bailey and Brayan Rocchio each had two of the team’s 11 hits — a complete turnaround for the AL Central champions after they managed just three runs and seven hits in the first two games of the series combined. Chicago won its first four games in a surprising postseason appearance after going 60-102 last year. It was backed by a frenzied crowd of 40,590 for the franchise’s first home playoff game since 2021, but there wasn’t much for the fans to cheer in the final innings. articles.title: Why did Jon Rahm quit LIV Golf? Reason behind $300 million star’s departure  explained
articles.summary: Jon Rahm is leaving LIV Golf.
articles.body: Jon Rahm is leaving LIV Golf. His lawyer, John Beck, told a New Jersey bankruptcy judge on Wednesday that the Spaniard reviewed the terms of the league's restructured version, called LIV 2.0, and found them unacceptable. Rahm signed in December 2023 and has won the league's season title three years running. The two-time major champion won't be part of the rebuilt tour, and both sides are working on a separation agreement. Money looks like the core issue, though neither has spelled out the terms.Why did Jon Rahm quit LIV Golf?Jon Rahm signed as the reigning Masters champion on a deal reported at more than $300 million. He won four LIV events, but the paychecks are where the trouble sits. LIV filed for Chapter 11 protection on Sept. 8, listing between $500 million and $1 billion in liabilities. Rahm tops the league's list of 30 largest unsecured claims at $7.5 million in past-due payments. He had also said he had no regrets about joining and wanted the league to be sustainable.The second version of the league looks nothing like the first. CEO Scott O'Neil has described 10 events with smaller purses, and said the league has to move away from a Saudi-style plan toward one that stands on its own. A proposed $300 million investment from BC Partners depends on conditions that include new player agreements. Nobody is forced to sign one. Players have no obligation to join LIV 2.0, even with multiyear deals on the books.Beck told the court the terms were "unacceptable as to him." No figures came with the statement. In May, Rahm had said he saw few ways out of a contract with several years left. The bankruptcy has since changed his circumstances, and it was later said both camps are in advanced talks on a consensual separation.What does Rahm's exit mean for LIV Golf and his next move?The PGA Tour door looks shut. CEO Brian Rolapp said on Sept. 15 that the tour has no plans to bring back the Returning Member Program, the route Brooks Koepka used to rejoin. Rahm, Bryson DeChambeau and Cameron Smith were the other names it could have covered.The DP World Tour is the other path. Rahm settled his dispute with the European circuit in May, which kept his membership and his Ryder Cup eligibility for next year. Where he plays in 2027 is not settled.The $300 million star has a thin major record since the move. He has one top-five and four top-10 finishes at majors, after three top-10s in 2023 alone.LIV has its own problems. Sergio Garcia has been released from his contract, and the deadline for current players to commit now sits at Oct. 25. It is not clear which players BC Partners requires for the deal to close, so Rahm's absence adds to the uncertainty. articles.title: A few inches – and a fan’s arms – separated Anthony Volpe from October heroics. Instead, the Yankees are swept by Tampa
articles.summary: Anthony Volpe thought he’d hit the game-tying home run as the Yankees tried to stave off elimination. But fan interference helped send New York home as Tampa sweeps.
articles.body: What a hero he would have been. The New York-born heir to Derek Jeter’s spot on the diamond, Anthony Volpe has become an unfortunate avatar of all the ways this iteration of the Yankees has failed to live up to the legacy set by the Jeter Era teams. The first-round draft pick turned homegrown source of hope-unrealized debuted in 2023 and has never had even an average offensive season. This year, he spent over a month demoted to the minors. He entered October with just two home runs. He’ll leave it that way, too. The Yankees season is over. They were swept by the Tampa Bay Rays – who also bested them in the division despite a bottom-three payroll compared to New York’s third-highest in baseball – in the American League Division Series. Blame belongs up and down the lineup as well as directed at the fallibility of human calf muscles. Ask the New York fans left disappointed, and they’ll say blame belongs higher up as well. Following the final out, the chant that rang out around Yankee Stadium was “Fire Aaron Boone!” But before that, for a moment in the sixth inning Wednesday night, it looked like Volpe may have at least staved off the reckoning, if not fully reversed the momentum back in the Yankees’ favor. Over two games in Tampa, the Rays had embarrassed the Yankees – nearly no hitting them in Game 1 and putting the ball in play and watching the errors ensue in Game 2. Back home in the Bronx with the Yanks’ backs against the wall, Volpe was given the start at short for the first time in the series. Before the game, Boone said he hoped Volpe would provide a “spark.” It wasn’t the worst plan. In the fourth, Volpe scored to tie the game at two. In the sixth, he came to the plate with two outs, a runner on, and the Yankees trailing by two. And then he did it – the storybook version of how that at bat would play out if this was about a guy who finally got his moment. Volpe sent the 1-0 pitch 357 feet to left field, over the outstretched glove of the Rays’ left fielder and … onto the outstretched arms of a navy blue-clad Yankee fan. It clanked awkwardly, not quite caught but deflected back into the stands. “It is up! It is out! It’s a home run!” the broadcast declared. Tie game. New life for the beleaguered Bombers. “Off the bat, I like the chances,” the Yankees captain, the sidelined Aaron Judge, said later of the pivotal play. His manager wasn’t as convinced. “I was a little concerned right away,” Boone said. “I wasn’t sure.” Neither were the umpires on the field, who sent it for a replay review. The slowed-down, side angle was clear: Fan interference. Volpe was awarded a double, driving in just one run to make the game 4-3 in favor of Tampa. It was the last scoring for either side on the night. “Seeing the replay and seeing it unfold, I thought they did the right thing,” Boone said. “I thought they got it right.” They did, and that’s the important part. It doesn’t matter that almost exactly 30 years ago Jeter himself hit a similar ball that was ruled a home run despite interference from a young fan. That home run, which was allowed to stand, tied an ALCS game that was eventually won in a postseason that was eventually a World Series championship that eventually started a dynasty. Could it have all hinged on that swing? On a ball that was only expected to be a home run in 12 out of 30 stadiums (the park where it was taking place not among them)? Maybe. But not likely. Even the most dedicated and determined Yankee fan would struggle to blame external forces for their elimination. It wasn’t a blown call. It wasn’t even really a game of inches. “We had more opportunities, we had a bunch more innings left,” Volpe said after the game was over, that same 4-3 scoreline in favor of the Rays. “We just didn’t come back.” “Ultimately we didn’t swing the bats enough in this series to move on,” Boone said. And so instead they’ll go home. Another season in the books without a new Yankee ring. Another winter of wondering whether it all could have been different, or if there’s something fundamentally rotten in the Bronx. It’s not the umpire’s fault or the fan’s fault they lost. It’s not Volpe’s fault either – not entirely or even predominantly or any more than anyone else in that lineup. He’s just the one left wondering – if he got another few inches on that fly ball – would he have been the hero?

articles.title: “We May Have to Score”: When Notre Dame’s Defense Took Over Against Stanford
articles.summary: Looking back at Notre Dame’s 2002 win over the Stanford Cardinal to get back the Legend’s Trophy.
articles.body:
Looking at the final score from Notre Dame's October 5, 2002 matchup against Stanford, you might assume the Irish had a relatively easy afternoon. Notre Dame won 31-7, improved to 5-0 in Tyrone Willingham's first season as head coach, and continued what was quickly becoming one of the biggest surprises of the college football season.

But anyone who watched the first half probably remembers things a little differently.

Notre Dame entered the game 4-0 for the first time since 1993 and was coming off a dramatic 21-17 victory over Michigan State. That win had provided one of the early memorable moments of the Willingham era when starting quarterback Carlyle Holiday injured his shoulder and walk-on Pat Dillingham came off the bench. With just over a minute remaining, Dillingham connected with Arnaz Battle for the game-winning touchdown.

One week later, the unlikely hero was suddenly Notre Dame's starting quarterback.

Dillingham would be making his first collegiate start against Stanford, which added another layer to an already interesting game. Willingham had spent seven seasons as Stanford's head coach before taking the Notre Dame job, meaning that many of the players standing on the opposite sideline were young men he had recruited and coached.

There were plenty of storylines. What Notre Dame needed, however, was simply to keep winning.

Early on, that proved more difficult than expected.

The Irish had opportunities almost immediately. After Stanford was forced to punt on its opening possession, Notre Dame moved to the Cardinal 34 before the drive stalled. Nick Setta's 51-yard field-goal attempt fell short. A bad snap on another Stanford punt soon gave Notre Dame the ball at the Cardinal 33, but a personal foul followed by a five-yard loss helped squander that opportunity as well.

Stanford eventually began moving the ball, but Notre Dame's defense held when the Cardinal reached the Irish 14, and a 37-yard field-goal attempt was blocked. Then it appeared Notre Dame had finally found the spark it needed when Vontez Duff returned a punt 92 yards for a touchdown.

Notre Dame was penalized for roughing the center, wiping the touchdown off the board and giving Stanford another opportunity. Willingham later called the penalty "unusual," which may have been one of the more diplomatic descriptions available to him at the time.

Stanford made the second chance count. Quarterback Chris Lewis connected with Teyo Johnson for a 14-yard touchdown, and the Cardinal led 7-0 at the end of the first quarter.

Notre Dame's defense made sure Stanford wouldn't do much more offensively, but the Irish offense continued to struggle to turn opportunities into points. A second-quarter drive finally reached the Stanford six before Setta kicked a field goal, sending Notre Dame into halftime trailing 7-3.

The most frustrating part was that Notre Dame had possessed the ball in Stanford territory on six of its seven first-half possessions.

And the Irish had three points to show for it.

Willingham would describe it as Notre Dame's worst half of the season, and defensive coordinator Kent Baer apparently came to an interesting conclusion while watching the offense struggle. He told his players, "We may have to score a touchdown here to win this thing."

As it turned out, his defense was listening.

First, however, the offense had to provide a little help.

Notre Dame's opening possession of the third quarter ended with a Dillingham interception, and another promising drive ended when Setta missed a 38-yard field goal. The Irish defense continued to keep Stanford pinned down, giving the offense good field position and another opportunity.

This time Notre Dame finally finished a drive.

The Irish marched 57 yards before Rashon Powers-Neal scored on a three-yard run, giving Notre Dame its first lead of the afternoon, 10-7, with 4:22 remaining in the third quarter.

And then the game changed almost instantly.

Two plays after the ensuing kickoff, Shane Walton intercepted a Lewis pass and returned it 18 yards for a touchdown. Just 24 seconds after Notre Dame had taken its first lead, the Irish were ahead 17-7.

Walton's interception was already his fifth of the season, but apparently the defense wasn't satisfied with one touchdown.

On Stanford's next possession, Lewis completed a pass to tight end Alex Smith. Courtney Watson wrestled the football away from him and took off in the opposite direction, returning it 34 yards for another Notre Dame touchdown.

Baer had told his defense it might need to score a touchdown.

In a span of just 3 minutes and 13 seconds, Notre Dame scored 21 points and transformed what had been a frustrating, uncomfortable afternoon into a 24-7 lead.

The defense still wasn't finished. On the first play of the fourth quarter, Gerome Sapp intercepted Lewis at the Stanford 45. Notre Dame's offense took advantage this time, using its ground game to move down the field before Ryan Grant scored from one yard out.

It was a remarkable turnaround considering how the afternoon had started. Notre Dame had trailed 7-3 at halftime, struggled repeatedly in Stanford territory and watched a 92-yard punt-return touchdown disappear because of a penalty. By the end of the game, the Irish had won by 24 points.

Dillingham's numbers in his first collegiate start weren't spectacular. He completed 14 of 27 passes for 129 yards and threw one interception, but he didn't need to be spectacular. Stanford coach Buddy Teevens credited Dillingham afterward for remaining composed, saying Notre Dame had allowed him to play within his strengths and that the players around him seemed confident in his ability to run the offense.

It certainly helped that Notre Dame could run the football.

The Irish finished with 249 rushing yards, led by Powers-Neal and Grant, who both topped the 100-yard mark. Willingham was particularly pleased with the performance of his offensive line, crediting the group for being physical, communicating well and putting themselves in the right positions throughout the afternoon.

But once again, the story of this Notre Dame team was its defense.

Through five games, the Irish defense had become remarkably good at doing more than simply stopping opponents. It was creating points. Against Stanford, Walton and Watson turned two turnovers directly into touchdowns, while Sapp's interception set up another score. When Notre Dame's offense needed time to find itself, the defense provided it.

That alone felt significant. The Irish hadn't started a season with five consecutive victories since 1993, and a team that had finished 5-6 the year before had already matched its entire 2001 win total.

Naturally, people were beginning to wonder just how far this team might go.

Willingham wasn't interested in joining the speculation.

"We'll just kindly take 5-0 and just keep going," he said afterward. "All I want to be is a team that plays the best the next Saturday afternoon. That's all I want."

There was also a quieter moment after the game that said something about just how unusual the afternoon had been for Notre Dame's new head coach.

As Willingham was conducting a television interview, Stanford quarterback Chris Lewis made his way through the group of reporters surrounding him. Willingham stopped the interview to greet his former player, embracing him and speaking briefly with him. Other Stanford players approached their former coach as he eventually made his way toward the tunnel.

For seven years, those had been Willingham's players.

Now he was walking away with Notre Dame at 5-0.

More than two decades later, the 31-7 score makes this game easy to overlook. It looks like a comfortable Notre Dame victory tucked into the middle of an undefeated start.

For one half, almost everything that could frustrate the Irish did. Drives stalled. Field goals were missed. A touchdown was erased. Stanford led at halftime. Notre Dame's backup quarterback was making his first start, and Willingham was trying to defeat the program he had left less than a year earlier.

Then Rashon Powers-Neal finally found the end zone, and Notre Dame's defense took it from there.

Kent Baer had suggested his defense might have to score a touchdown to win.

articles.title: Official: Andrea Medina receives sought-after award from fans after incredible start to life in Manchester
articles.summary: Manchester United Women have turned their season around.The Red Devils lost their first two league games of the season against London City Lionesses and Chel...
articles.body:
Manchester United Women have turned their season around.

The Red Devils lost their first two league games of the season against London City Lionesses and Chelsea.

A spirited draw away to Arsenal seemed to boost confidence, and they won their next four matches on the trot.

This included smashing Sheffield United 10-1 in the cup and also narrowly defeating arch-rivals Liverpool 1-0.

United brought in four players this summer, with all three outfield players—Rebeca Bernal, Monica Jusu Bah and Andrea Medina—getting on the scoresheet.

Nonetheless, the best signing to date has certainly been the Spanish star, Medina.

She joined from Atlético Madrid on a free transfer and has taken to life at the Progress with Unity Stadium like a duck to water.

Despite being a full-back by trade, Medina has recently been asked by coach Eva Olid to play in an attacking winger role, and the move has worked out a treat so far.

Medina scored her first goal for the club recently with a wonderful solo effort against West Ham United last month.

The club's official website states, "Andrea Medina has deservedly won the Manchester United Women Player of the Month award for September."

It continues, "the Spaniard has enjoyed a superb start to life with the Reds, starting all four of our league outings – twice in a relatively unfamiliar left-wing role."

The 22-year-old also won successive player of the match awards versus Arsenal and West Ham in the league.

articles.title: The 300mph motorsport where women keep winning
articles.summary: Top Fuel drag racing is the only elite motorsport class where women frequently beat men to major titles.
articles.body:
Like "being shot out of a cannon" is the closest comparison that driver Susanne Callin can come up with for the extreme motorsport she competes in.

She is a two-time European champion in Top Fuel drag racing - often described as the fastest sport on the planet.

Races begin with a bone-shaking roar, as the world's fastest-accelerating cars leave the starting line, flames bursting out of their exhaust pipes.

The cars surge to more than 300mph (483km/h) in races that last just four seconds, with drivers experiencing more g-force than an astronaut launching into space.

It is the only elite class of motorsport where women frequently beat men to major titles.

Women have won seven out of the past nine European Championships, while, until recently, female US driver Brittany Force held the world speed record in the sport. In comparison, it is 50 years since a woman even competed in a Formula 1 Grand Prix race.

Women account for about 10% of participants across motorsport, and just 4% of elite drivers, according to campaign group More Than Equal. However, they made up 20% of the drivers competing in this year's US and European Top Fuel seasons.

So why is this high-velocity motorsport bucking the trend?

More Than Equal has described drag racing as "the most gender-equal motorsport in the world". Top Fuel is its most extreme form, named in reference to the powerful nitromethane fuel the cars run on.

Races take place on a straight track, just 1,000 feet (305 metres) long. Usually, two cars race each other. The intense g-force hits in the first second of the race, as the cars go from stationary to 100mph, with a second gut punch following as the clutch fully engages about half-way through.

It can look terrifying. The adrenalin rush is "extremely addictive", Swedish driver Callin, aged 43, tells BBC Global Women. Concern over the risks "is always there" she says, but "the safety really does work". Drivers are highly protected and safety precautions have been boosted further after fatal crashes in nitromethane-fuelled cars in 2004 and 2008, with races reduced in length.

Even just watching from the stands is a visceral experience, with vibrations shaking your body and the ground. Spectators are advised to wear ear defenders - the noise is comparable in decibels to standing next to a fighter jet taking off.

The highest official speed ever reached in a Top Fuel drag race is over 346mph, compared to 231mph in a Formula 1 Grand Prix. Brakes alone cannot slow the cars fast enough, so parachutes are deployed from the car's rear at the finish. The abrupt halt is "like someone kicking you in the chest", says Callin. "You lose your breath."

Top Fuel drivers need lightning-fast reactions and the physical endurance to withstand the intense forces. Precision driving skills are crucial as constant tiny adjustments are needed to keep the car on track.

"It has to be instant reactions with everything," says Callin. "By the time you've thought about it, it's too late… You really have to be one with the car."

And drivers need sheer guts. As Callin's rival and friend, 32-year-old Swiss driver Jndia Erbacher, jokingly tells the BBC - it takes "balls".

Callin clinched her second successive European Top Fuel title in September at the Santa Pod drag strip near Northampton. It is the fourth year in a row that a female driver has won the title. Meanwhile in the US, the record-setting Brittany Force won the US championship - run by the National Hot Rod Association (NHRA) - in both 2017 and 2022.

Drag racing is "highly unusual" among motorsports, says Fran Longstaff, chief innovation officer at More Than Equal, which supports and campaigns for women in motorsports.

Seeing women competing and winning in the sport has become "normalised rather than treated as exceptional", she says, including with "sustained success" in Top Fuel.

Research she co-led into why drag racing leads the way for equality in motorsport did not identify physical or biological factors, she says.

Instead, she points to a "continuous stream of visible female role models", as well as the sport's "accessible grassroots structure, junior programmes, open pits and family-oriented, collaborative culture".

In drag racing, points out Callin, women started winning major races "decades and decades ago".

The best known is Shirley Muldowney, dubbed the "first lady" of drag racing. The first woman to gain a Top Fuel licence, Muldowney won the NHRA championship in 1977 and went on to become the first driver to win three titles, with further wins in 1980 and 1982.

She had to battle to be allowed to compete at high levels, and faced hostility at times from other competitors and fans, but is now lauded for her perseverance.

When the BBC spent time with Callin in the pits between races at Santa Pod, surrounded by roaring engines and the smell of burning rubber, she signed autographs for fans - young and old, male and female - as her team prepared her car.

"I never feel I've been underestimated or treated badly for being a woman - never," Callin says.

This is in stark contrast to the experiences of women seeking to enter Formula 1. Young female drivers have spoken about being deliberately pushed off karting tracks by male competitors, and facing sexist comments in person or online.

More Than Equal's research also highlights a close-knit, family-oriented, collaborative culture in drag racing.

Like many top drag racers, Callin is from a racing family. She has been involved since childhood, following in the footsteps of her father and uncle, who both raced competitively.

Similarly, Erbacher's father Urs was a three-time European Top Fuel champion. And Brittany Force is the daughter of John Force, who holds 16 NHRA drag racing titles.

The 300mph motorsport where women keep winning

Watch the full documentary following Susanne Callin as she bids to retain her European Top Fuel title

Female drivers have also shown that success is possible in Top Fuel in the years after having children.

Callin took a break for more than a decade to raise her daughter and stepdaughters. It was when she returned, aged 35, that her career really began to flourish. Similarly, Finnish driver Anita Mäkelä has won the European championship four times – three of them after a six-year break focusing on her children and running her family's chicken farm.

For Callin, racing is ingrained in family life.

Her dad is still part of her team. Her husband, Keith Bartlett - sometimes referred to as the "godfather" of UK drag racing - runs Santa Pod Raceway. Two of their daughters were driving junior dragsters at 80mph before they were old enough to sit a standard driving test. The youngest, Jacqueline, is now 19 and racing in adult classes.

The culture is collaborative, despite fierce competition - evident at last year's championship, when Erbacher offered Callin spare parts after her car was damaged.

"We hate each other at the starting line, but we love each other at the finish line," Erbacher says.

Asked about safety, both Callin and Erbacher talk about having "respect" for the car and the risks.

Over the years, strict procedures and regulations in Top Fuel have evolved to improve safety.

Drivers wear fire-resistant suits and sit in highly protected cockpits. Even after dramatic accidents, drivers in many cases escape relatively unscathed. This includes Callin, who has had two major crashes, suffering a concussion and a bruised collar bone, but no lasting injuries.

She says serious accidents are a "very small percentage". Even so, she is still not sure she would be comfortable if her daughter wanted to race in Top Fuel, with its extreme speeds.

Erbacher says her father initially refused to let her race, but relented when she declared she would do it with or without his help. He now manages her team.

More Than Equal also points out that the financial barriers to participating in drag racing are lower than for some other motorsports.

It takes millions of pounds to reach Formula 1, requiring high levels of sponsorship. Elite drag racing is also expensive, but not on the same scale. At the lowest levels, accessible racing events called "track days" take place, where participants can turn up and drive their own ordinary cars.

In the biggest Top Fuel championships, drivers race for themselves and earn points based on how they perform against their competitors. The European championship consists of four events - two in the UK, and one each in Germany and Sweden - in which each driver takes part in six races. Prize funds are limited, mostly serving as a contribution towards costs.

The US championship is on a larger scale, with 20 events across the country. The NHRA has not published a breakdown of prize money, but according to drag racing website Competition Plus, there is $500,000 (£378,000) for the 2026 winner, and significant pots for winners of individual events throughout the season.

The US, Europe and Australia have all seen female drag racing champions, but in other parts of the world, the sport is less well established, Top Fuel is rare and the picture is more varied. Individual women are breaking barriers across a range of different motorsports, and in some countries female drivers are carving out space in drag racing.

Women have begun to make an impact in Brazil's popular drag racing scene, including Fabiola Dal Bo who has held a category record in recent years. A team in South Africa hosts all-female drag races, while the popular reality TV show The Fastest in Arabic has raised the profile of women racers in the Middle East.

In India, 35-year-old Uvashri Kannadasan Balajeyanthi has clinched victories over male rivals in India's major drag racing series, Valley Run, with wins across three different categories in events from 2022 to 2024.

Known as Octy Girl in reference to the modified Skoda Octavia she first raced in, she tells the BBC she has "mixed feelings" when her achievements are met with surprise: "Why do they have to get shocked? Anyone can drive, right?" But she adds "sometimes I feel proud… I'm breaking the barrier of being in a male-dominated sport".

Back in Europe, however, Callin says being a woman on the drag strip is "super-normal".

She describes winning the European championship two years running as a "massive achievement". And she is already looking towards her next goal: becoming the first person, male or female, to win the title three years in a row.

This is part of the Global Women series from the BBC World Service, sharing untold and important stories from around the globe

articles.title: Aaron Judge looking forward to Yankees front office's response to another playoff exit
articles.summary: After the Yankees suffered another early playoff exit following their Game 3 loss to the Rays, Aaron Judge was asked about the front office and what he wants...
articles.body:
It's another season without a World Series championship for Aaron Judge.

The Yankees captain, who most certainly will have his No. 99 retired soon after he calls it quits, will have to wait at least another year for his first chance to win gold. This postseason was especially hard for Judge, who had to sit out both the Wild Card Series and ALDS due to a calf injury. He was in the dugout as the Yankees offense mustered just five runs while being swept by the Rays at home in Game 3 of the ALDS.

"It's always tough," Judge said after the loss. "Anytime you're not the last team standing, and lose at home like that, three straight games, it's definitely difficult. It hurts. You want to be out there, all the rehab, all the work, coming here early, staying late. Any time you're banged up, you're trying to get back out there as soon as you can. Hurts not getting a chance to be out there and battling."

Despite not being in the lineup, Judge said he liked the 2026 Yankees' chances in the postseason, as he's said in years past. But this year, from the pitching staff anchored by likely Cy Young winner Cam Schlittler and rounded out by veterans Gerrit Cole, Max Fried and Carlos Rodon, to young hitters Spencer Jones and George Lombard Jr. stepping up, the three-time MVP felt there was enough in the clubhouse to go far.

So, why can't the Yankees get over the hump? While Judge didn't give specifics, he said he and his teammates were not satisfied with this result.

Then Judge was asked directly about his thoughts on what he thinks the response from GM Brian Cashman and owner Hal Steinbrenner should be following another postseason loss, and the captain answered honestly.

"We're the Yankees. I feel like they should go all-in and do what they need to do," Judge said. "If we've got holes, if it's finding certain players or personnel, whatever we need, you got to go out there and get it. That's why I signed back here to play with the Yankees is to fight for a championship every single year and go all-in. That's what I do every offseason, is get ready to give this team and this city everything I got. And I expect them to do the same."

When he was asked if he felt they went "all-in," Judge said he will leave the moves to the front office and will control what he can control. But when a follow-up asked if he felt the front office went "all-in enough," Judge took a beat before responding.

"It's tough to say. I want to trade for everybody, sign everybody every single year, but I know that's not realistic," he said. "They give us a winning team every single year, but that's not good enough here in New York. We're the Yankees. You've got to go out there and expect championships and go all-in every year. I'm excited to see what they do."

articles.title: David Sánchez se planta ante el interés del Bayern por Dani Olmo: "Ni por 100 millones"
articles.standfirst: El presentador de Despierta San Francisco defiende en La Tribu la continuidad del internacional español en el Barcelona y pide a Flick que convenza a Deco y Laporta para evitar su salida
articles.summary: El presentador de Despierta San Francisco defiende en La Tribu la continuidad del internacional español en el Barcelona y pide a Flick que convenza a Deco y Laporta para evitar su salida
articles.body: El futuro de Dani Olmo vuelve a estar en el centro del debate azulgrana. Según ha explicado David Sánchez en La Tribu de Radio MARCA, desde Alemania apuntan a un interés del Bayern de Múnich por hacerse con los servicios del futbolista del Barcelona. Una operación que podría rondar los 90 millones de euros y ante la que el periodista ha mostrado su oposición. "Leo por Alemania que hay mucho interés por parte del Bayern de Múnich para intentar la contratación de Dani Olmo de cara al mercado de invierno y si no de cara a la próxima temporada", ha comenzado explicando David Sánchez, antes de añadir que "se dice en Alemania que el conjunto bávaro estaría dispuesto a pagar en torno a 90 millones de euros". El periodista reconoce que la situación económica del Barcelona podría favorecer una operación de estas características: "Sé que es mucha pasta y que es un dinero que el Barcelona, tal y como tiene las arcas, estaría muy por la labor de aceptarlos". Sin embargo, David Sánchez considera que el proyecto deportivo debe estar por encima de cualquier oferta y confía en que el técnico alemán intervenga para evitar la salida del futbolista. "Espero que Hansi Flick vuelva a convencer a Deco y a Laporta que esto trata de ganar títulos y es mucho más fácil ganarlos con los buenos que con los no tan buenos", ha asegurado. Además, ha restado importancia al hecho de que Dani Olmo no tenga el mismo protagonismo en el Barcelona que en la selección española: "Me da igual. Para ganar una Liga, una Champions, una Copa, una Supercopa y lo que se ponga por delante, tienes que tener no un gran equipo". David Sánchez ha insistido en la importancia de contar con una plantilla amplia y de calidad para competir por todos los títulos. "Tienes que tener una grandísima plantilla y el Barcelona es mejor teniendo en el mismo equipo a Fermín, a Pedri y a Dani Olmo", ha defendido. Por último, el periodista ha recordado el esfuerzo que hizo el futbolista para regresar al club azulgrana y ha lanzado un mensaje contundente a quienes puedan estar interesados en su fichaje. "Es un jugador de la cantera de Can Barça que hizo un esfuerzo para volver a jugar en Barcelona y el Barcelona ahora no lo puede vender ni por 70, ni por 80, ni por 90, ni por 100. Si lo quieren, la cláusula", ha sentenciado. Y ha cerrado su intervención con una postura clara sobre el futuro del internacional español: "Si no, Dani Olmo se tiene y se debe de quedar en Barcelona".

articles.title: ‘I’m Going To Make History’ – Rifdean Masdor Plots World Title Upset Over Nadaka Yoshinari At ONE SAMURAI 4
articles.summary: The Malaysian knockout artist is ready to shake up Tokyo's Ariake Arena with the performance of a lifetime on October 17.
articles.body:
Rifdean "Magic Boy" Masdor has waited nearly half a decade to share the global stage with reigning ONE Atomweight Muay Thai World Champion Nadaka Yoshinari , and he intends to make the most of the occasion.

The Malaysian knockout artist challenges the Japanese divisional king in the co-main event of the loaded ONE SAMURAI 4 , which emanates live from the historic Ariake Arena in Tokyo, Japan, on Saturday, October 17.

Rifdean enjoys a five-fight winning streak, capped by a 94-second knockout of Javad Mozafari at The Inner Circle 19 that secured him the life-changing US$100,000 main roster contract .

There is no bigger way to introduce himself than through a World Title opportunity against the very man he has spent years wanting to face.

The Sor Sommai and Sor Kitrungroj warrior said:

"After seven wins in ONE Championship, I'm ready to fight Nadaka. I've genuinely wanted to fight Nadaka for a long time already. I've been closely following Nadaka for four years now. "This fight is going to be huge because Nadaka has never lost yet, but I'm going to make him lose. I'm going to make history. I'm going to be the first person to hand him a loss."

"After seven wins in ONE Championship, I'm ready to fight Nadaka. I've genuinely wanted to fight Nadaka for a long time already. I've been closely following Nadaka for four years now.

"This fight is going to be huge because Nadaka has never lost yet, but I'm going to make him lose. I'm going to make history. I'm going to be the first person to hand him a loss."

Indeed, since calling ONE Championship home, Nadaka has been nothing short of spectacular. A dominant 6-0 tenure in the organization has extended his active winning streak to 42 in succession, a run built over the past seven years.

Most recently, the Eiwa Sports Gym affiliate opened his kickboxing account with a striking clinic against Har Ling Om in the main event of ONE SAMURAI 3 in Yokohama, Japan.

Speed, power, and movement all factor into what makes the Japanese megastar the gold standard of the division, but his sharp tactical awareness is what truly separates him from the rest. "Magic Boy," however, believes he carries the exact tools needed to solve that puzzle.

"Nadaka is very, very good. He's a fighter who's fast, smart, and strong. He has all of it, really. But I have power. Nadaka doesn't have power. He only has speed and technical IQ. I feel like I can beat him with my power, but I shouldn't go full power all the time. It needs the right timing and power. "And a lot of people [have also said that] Nadaka has good IQ, while I don't because I'm just strong at throwing punches and kicks. But I believe this fight against him will be IQ versus IQ."

Given that read on the matchup, Rifdean is not predicting a quick finish from either side at ONE SAMURAI 4.

Despite owning five finishes in ONE, the 23-year-old Malaysian expects this one to require more patience than his typical night out, with the final decision coming down to small margins rather than a single decisive blow.

"No one's getting knocked out in this fight because I'm going to make it different this time. We can't just fight him with brute strength. If we fight him with strength alone, we might get caught out. So, maybe this fight ends in a split decision. "I agree with what people think of Nadaka. He is the best fighter in the world right now. But God willing, he's about to fight the best too, Rifdean Masdor. If I win against him, I'm the best in the world."

Rifdean Carries A Nation's Dream With Him

Beating the ever-dominant Nadaka Yoshinari would do more than just hand the Japanese titan his first defeat since July 2019.

It would make Rifdean Masdor the new ONE Atomweight Muay Thai World Champion, and only the second martial artist from Malaysia to claim the sport's most coveted prize.

Earlier this year, Aliff Sor Dechapan made history as the first to do so when he knocked out the legendary Sam-A Gaiyanghadao at The Inner Circle 23 . Three months later, "Magic Boy" is eager to give his country another milestone worth celebrating.

"I will bring that belt back for my Malaysian people. Then, after I win, I'll bring the celebration back to Malaysia, for the people of Malaysia and Sarawak. If I become the Atomweight World Champion, I'd be so happy. It means that my dream would have come true."

As massive as that accomplishment would be, Rifdean is careful not to treat it as the finish line.

In his mind, claiming the divisional gold would mark the beginning of something far bigger, and he already has a clear sense of what that bigger picture looks like for both himself and his country.

"[If I become the World Champion], it will just be the starting point. It's a journey to go even further, for me to step into the future. This is not just a belt. It's an important [accolade] for us. "We want to be the best on the world stage. But it's not easy either. But if we get that title in ONE Championship, people will recognize us, and we'll go far."
